When the attack begins everybody makes for their craft to get the heck out of Dodge, but your intentions are different; your ship the Theresa May might be a bulky, rusted piece of obsolete space junk but she's also armed to the metaphorical teeth. Time to fire up the systems, sling your craft skywards and blast some nasties because... well, reasons. Look, this is a shoot 'em up and nobody reads the instructions for these things unless it's to kill time during loading so I'm surprised you're still paying any attention at this point!

177281.overview:
It's the year 2304 and, after centuries of negotiation, diplomacy and peace unexpectedly collapse, an intergalactic war has broken out; outlying worlds of the Galactic Federation have already found themselves coming under fire from the Repugnant Swarm who have laid waste to cities and farmland alike. The next target of the Swarm's ire on their way to the centre of our galactic hub and the source of that insult is Stercore XD, an artificial "world" constructed in deep space used as a refuelling point for cargo craft delivering supplies to the federation's outlying colonies.

When the attack begins everybody makes for their craft to get the heck out of Dodge, but your intentions are different; your ship the Theresa May might be a bulky, rusted piece of obsolete space junk but she's also armed to the metaphorical teeth. Time to fire up the systems, sling your craft skywards and blast some nasties because... well, reasons. Look, this is a shoot 'em up and nobody reads the instructions for these things unless it's to kill time during loading so I'm surprised you're still paying any attention at this point!


This is not so much a sequel to the original Stercore 64 as it is a reworked version with updated graphics, and was developed for the RGCD C64 16KB Cartridge Game Development Competition 2019.

177325.overview: While sailing, you notice a figure hobbling on a wooden leg and waving for you to land on the beach. You beach your sailboat and disembark but the person has vanished without leaving a trace in the sands. Can you escape the island, avoid any nasty volcano burns and live to spend the hidden treasure?

177415.overview:
Shoikan\Crux is a game of logic that will not fail to thrill you. The concept is very simple: you have to arrange all the pieces on the screen so that at the end they are in the identical position (both in color and in place) to that indicated at the bottom. 

Published in both Magic Disk 64 1991/09 and in All C64 n.1 (1992/1993).

177490.overview: A dueling game for 2 players only.

177493.overview: An avoid it game. Maneuver your helo through the maze without hitting the sides, avoid the falling rocks and make it to the exit.

177506.overview: Shredz64 is a game modelled against the mechanics of Guitar Hero to play music on a guitar controller. Players need to match notes in five columns, each with its own colour, against the rhythm and melody of the music. Doing well increases the applause meter and when it runs out the game is over. Similar to Guitar Hero's star power, perfect parts increase a shredocity meter, allowing the player to lift the guitar, turning the screen border red and scoring additional points. The screen only shows the notes in a pseudo 3D fashion, with nothing else in the background. The game makes use of the PSX64 interface that connects PlayStation controllers to computers that use a DB9 port, and the Commodore 64 pin configuration. For the PlayStation 2 guitar controller, this does not only include button presses, but the whammy bar, strumming and lifting as well. The initial game was released with ten instrumental songs divided over different difficulty levels. It includes a mix of game soundtracks (Zelda, Zak McKracken), movie soundtracks (Beverly Hills Cop, Ghostbusters) and renditions of popular songs (Hotel California, Lick My Guitar). Players can add their own SID files to the game and record custom notes. There are separate PAL and NTSC versions, and high score tracking is included.

177507.overview:
Sieg in Afrika is a tactical war simulation based upon the North African campaign between the Axis and Allied forces during World War II. Italy declared war on Great Britain and France on June 10, 1940. Mussolini immediately ordered his troops in Libya to advance into Egypt. With more that ten divisions in North Africa to the three Allied divisions, he foresaw no difficulties the Western desert forces in detail. Designed for 1 - 2 players, each player controls the major land forces of either the Axis or Allied forces. A computer opponent is available for 1-player games. The viewpoint is from a corps level commander, and the player assigns movement and combat tasks for those groups, and responds to operational events.

The game is text-only, and came with a board and physical pieces to allow the player to keep track of the location of theirs and enemy units. All games begin in in June 1940, and progresses in 1 month intervals. Each break allows the player to input new commands for their forces. Each phase has an intelligence gathering component and a second component where troop orders can be given. Forces can be instructed to attack, break off, engage & destroy, hold, leaguer, move, rush, or search & sweep a location. The player must contend with limited fuel, food, and ammunition, and must make tactical decisions as to which units to reinforce. At the end of each turn, the player receives radio reports from their troops and main command regarding current enemy troop locations and combat results.

177508.overview:
One of the early Sierra On-Line releases, this game lets you design your own boxer before taking him/her/it to the ring. You can play as a black or a white guy, a cartoonish character or a kangaroo (!).
Three play modes exist:
Completely interactive: You control your fighter's every move
Coaching: You tell your fighter how to fight (aggressive, jabbing, defensive, etc.) in between rounds
Completely simulated: The computer does all the fighting
Stats are input in text variables, allowing you to not only customize your boxer very specifically (reach, height, weight, etc.) but also recreate some of history's best fighters and pit them together in a simulation.
Two-player mode supported.

177512.overview: Control your droid up and down the screen, avoiding the security bots. Collect disks to disable a computer virus, which threatens to wipe out every machine in the world. Once all disks have been collected, you will move on to the next level.

177513.overview: A text adventure that takes you from a deserted metro station to the mysterious sign of the Sphinx. Aficionados of the arcade, disciples of doom, students of the sinister and masters of the macabre have a new home in the future dark age of dying earth. From the dark shrines of bizarre cults to the ruins of ancient and modern civilizations, you can trace fragments of forgotten knowledge to the final secrets at the Crimson Altar.

177530.overview:
A weird miscellaneous game touted as, "a compendium of useless but diverting stuff for you and your 64. Another waste of your precious time..." 
Enjoy? an annoying repetitions message, read Sillydata, browse a Sillypoem, react to a Sillycrisis or go back to Reality™ if you must.

177531.overview:
Silva Pod is a trippy twist on Breakout\Arkanoid. Easy to beat by yourself, way more interesting to play with a friend.

Developed by Nicolas Star and published in  Magic Disk 64 1996/01.

177535.overview: In the game simulating some kind of golf you should complete the course consisting of 18 stages, putting the ball into the hole with as less strokes of the ball as possible. Each stage is presented on one screen in top-down view, it has a different shape, and different obstacles or gates are set to be avoided or passed through. Setting the ball in the field, you should select the direction and power of the stroke. The points at the end of each stage are calculated as subtraction of made strokes and pre-defined ones different for each stage. The winner is a golfer with a lowest number of points. The number of players (1-4), their names, and courses may be adjusted before the start. In multiplayer mode, each player strikes their balls in the separate fields in turns.

177536.overview:
Single Extreme Freedom was to be a strategic game developed by Alice Software Studio from between 1992 and 1994. It featured action and interactive fiction using a turn-based engine for two players where you play the King of Soregno and Saratosa in a fight against each other. 
 
In the game itself, the screen is divided into portions, which can be scrolled from right to left – the map; the hot spots of the events mentioned above are also bearing the name of their fictitious cities and ports. Between these lands, the players can move troops and ammunition, which can be traded, or navigate ships in the coastal area between. Throughout the game, there are various distractions which sometimes require the player to read a newspaper, or to bear children during that time. One aspect is that if you don’t have a child and if a king dies without an heir, then the game is over. There are three different periods in the kingdom’s history and each has its own text handler, players can also choose the destination at the beginning of the game and other conditions.

177537.overview: A "dueling" game for one person. Shoot the robot before he* shoots you. A game of the "Cassette 50" collection.

177538.overview:
Sir Ababol is a 2D platform game about Sir Ababol, a young crusader from Manchester City who lives in the 11th century. He witnesses the courage of St. George from Capadocia against the infidels and stumbles over a rock, falling into the Alcoraz River that carries him to the Monegros' Desert. When he wakes up he realizes he has lost his sword. He asks a farmer about the sword and is directed to a land full of ababol flowers. He is confused, but believes the red flowers may be tied to recovering his sword and decides to collect them, hoping to then continue his journey to Jerusalem. 

The game consists of a single, large level that comprises many single-screen rooms. The player can explore freely as the rooms are linked horizontally and vertically. To win the game 25 red flowers have to be collected in any order and then the game is won right away. Sir Ababol can move around and jump. He has no means to attack enemies and creatures and has to avoid them. Water is also a hazard. 

Sometimes keys need to be picked up to open doors to continue to a next section. Sir Ababol has a large amount of health with a single life. He can sustain more than one hundred hits, but life is drained quickly when in water or in an enemy's path. Health also counts down over time, acting as a time limit to complete the game. Some screens contain chicken to restore some health.

177539.overview:
A puzzle game created by Thomas Kemmer and published in Magic Disk 64 1991/10. For everyone for whom Manta Mania was too undemanding, or who do not want to deal with manta rays on principle, SIX is certainly the right place. SIX is a pure mind game and is about symbols and colors, like so many mind games. What is really new is the clever combination of different game ideas from well-known board and computer games that already exist. But read for yourself. .

You can play SIX either in pairs, namely in CHALLENGE mode, or alone in SOLITAIR mode. No matter how you play, the rules are the same. The computer gives you a stone that you have to place on the playing field. It's still very easy with the first stone, because it can be placed anywhere. For all other stones, you must now make sure that the stone matches all of its neighbors in pattern or color (or both). Otherwise you cannot get rid of the stone - and time is ticking inexorably! 

There are points for each stone placed. You will receive bonus points if you are able to fill a row or column. Most points are awarded if the row consists of only one color. A full row is then deleted to give the game more space. (We already know that from Tetris!) The winner is the one who can achieve the most points - the only thing in common with Manta Mania.

177541.overview: A game of skill and logic using six letter words.

177546.overview: Surf the bowl, avoid obstacles, do the tricks and score better than your opponent or your own best efforts. Published in Italy as Skate Board in Play on tape Nuova serie - American Games.

177547.overview: A scrolling screen platformer originally released into the Minigame Competition 2003 - 4K Category.

177553.overview: A sport skeet shooting game released as part of "Wild Kingdom" game pack and a part of "Sports Spectacular" game pack (re-release only).

177604.overview: A set of games intended to build important skills including: Speed Reader, Typing Tutor, Decision Maker and Memory Builder.  Released as part of "Commodore Pro-Pak" game pack.

177605.overview: A timed slalom skiing game, hit the gates as fast as you can.

177608.overview: Skidmarx is a simplified early version of Skidmarks, and is a racing game for up to two players. The race takes place on a single screen track. The first car that complete designated number of laps win the race. A few types of cars are available, number of tracks and color of vehicles are fully adjustable.

177618.overview: A "Commodore Home Planetarium" where you can learn about the stars. The magic of microelectronics has made it possible to have an accurate model of the universe in your own home at a modest cost. The awesome computations and enormous amounts of data are handled quickly and efficiently by your Commodore 64 computer. All you have to do is select your exploration commands and Sky Travel will return the information in pictorial form, directly on your screen - and in bright colors at that!

177622.overview: Something a bit bizarre. Drive around a very big car park\garage collecting gold and fuel while avoiding tacks and oil blobs. A fun one.

177633.overview: An action game with music by Chris Ammermüller and published in Game On 1990/12. Avoid the space hazards: rocks, comets, space stations, shields and platforms to continue moving forward. If you crash you start over at the beginning of the level. See if you can pass the tenth level and complete the mission.

177635.overview: Published in 64'er Sonderheft 42. Race as fast as you dare but avoid the black blocks and stay on the safe path. The crowning glory of every pilot's training: a low-level flight over an unknown spaceship. Only the best pilots avoid all obstacles in time. Will you be accepted into the galactic elite troop? Joystick acrobats get their money's worth with Sky Run. Daring maneuvers and a good eye are the prerequisites for surviving in the fast-paced race against time. Training to become a combat ship pilot usually takes three years. The task given in the final exam is not easy. After being dropped from a mother ship, you race your glider just above the surface of a training ship. Right from the start it is important to keep your eyes open and the control stick (joystick) firmly in your hands.

177639.overview: Move your figure to be able to roll through the advancing gates in this single player action game from Elwood Computer, published in 1983. Released in the UK as part of the Golden Oldies compilation.

177663.overview: A head to head shooter for you and a friend to play together and published in 64'er Sonderheft 49.

177664.overview:
Slater Man is a side-scrolling platform game. The goal of the game is to gather all the stars knocked down during the titular hero's careless ride across the galaxy. The game features 40 levels where the player must collect a specified number of stars and reach the end of the level to advance to the next planet before the time runs out. The task is complicated by numerous animals. Contact with them means certain death. The hostile creatures may be killed with unlimited arrows.

An unofficial English translated version was released the same year as the original release by Fantastic 4 Cracking Group.

177665.overview: Sled down the hill as fast as you can, but you must avoid all the berms or your sled will surely topple and bring you to a crashing halt. Released as part of the "Wild Kingdom" game pack.

177666.overview: Lady MacBeth - "To bed, to bed! There's knocking at the gate: come, come, come come, give me your hand. What's done cannot be undone. To bed, to bed, to bed!" Push the blocks around to form images.

177669.overview: You are a hungry ectoplasmic ghost. Catch the food, avoid the bombs. Remember a closed mouth gathers no food, or bombs!

177670.overview: A sliding puzzle game published in both 64'er Top-Spiele #3 and in 64'er 1998/03.

177671.overview:
Sliding Block Puzzles is a series of sliding block games for multiple systems.

The player chooses the difficulty level (ie. the number of columns and rows), as well as the image they wish to solving using a sliding block puzzle. There are 4 puzzle images.

177673.overview: Your Uncle Silas lives in a run down large house with lots of hazards everywhere. The problem you have though is that your Uncle sleepwalks and with all those obstacles scattered around you need to stop him from hitting the hazards so he doesn't wake up and suffer from a mental trauma. First you need to find him in this large house. Once your Uncle is located the only way to help him back to bed is to suffer the hazards yourself. While hurting yourself you can stand in front of Silas to send him the direction to bed. He must be returned to bed before the time runs out. Sleepwalker is a one-player, flick-screen game. On the screen you can see each room with the various hazards scattered around like cables, tacks and dynamite. Also on the screen is your score and a large clock showing your time left. The joystick is used to control your character.

177675.overview: A simple boxing game with various opponents. Released as part of the "C64/128 Battle Pack".

177676.overview:
A platforming game created by Roberto Barondi and Published in New Special Playgames N°09 (Maggio 1988) supplement: Games Commodore 64 N°1. 

The protagonist of this story is Slynky the curious sneak thief found a map of a place near his house in which a golden statuette is buried. Armed with a pick-axe and a shovel he begins the search for the statuette knowing he must avoid the undead that haunt the place and all manner of underground hazards.

177682.overview: A platformer originally made with "The Games Creator" and published in Hit Parade 64 N°32 (03/1989), Hit Parade 64 N°65 (03/1992).

177710.overview: A Pac Man style collect-em-up game for 1 to 4 players.

177711.overview:
A pong\airhockey type competition game where you make points by smashing the ball into the goal of your opponent. The call can be deviated by different objects in the field. The fire button will increase your speed but you have limited energy to strike a balance. Defend your goal while various beings wander around the screen, they can be destroyed in a hit but will unpredictably deflect the ball. A colored square may appear and hitting it can add some special effects such as immobilizing the opponent, allowing you to catch the ball, increase speed or reversing your controls!

Published as Affronto in Italy in Tutto C64 n.5 (1992/1993) and in Formula 64 n.106.

177713.overview: An 'avoid it" style action game published in 64'er Sonderheft 97. "Smash-Ball": Without warning, a very rich banker planet explodes in space. Collect all the money bags that are whizzing through the universe without getting hit by meteorite parts! The news spread like wildfire: Suddenly and without warning, the planet Bankonia in the Hyponid system had exploded! Millions of tiny fragments of meteorites race towards the neighboring planet Ballonia! The Ballonians read the headlines: A monstrous meteorite had grazed Bankonia and crumbled the planet into millions of pieces which are approaching Ballonia's orbit. Sirens wail, reconnaissance planes take to the skies, the spherical residents of Ballonia run back and forth like a startled swarm of bees — except for one, who stays cool: Smash, a yellow-skinned Ballonian who works as a garbage collector is our only hope!

177715.overview: A crude game of breakout using PETSCII graphics and written in BASIC. This is a game of the "Cassette 50" collection.

177716.overview: A game created with the Breakout Construction Kit, which would normally make this a homebrew but then it was Published in Commodore Format magazine.

177718.overview: A Snake\Worm game published in both 64'er 1991/04, and in 64'er Sonderheft 79. Do you like snakes, do you even like them to eat? That is your task in this game by Jürgen Graser and  Lauda-Könlgshofen. The game consists of biscuits imprisoning eight snakes. Your smiley (bottom right) must now try to eat all the snakes. However, this is only possible for him. y/when he has eaten all the cookies beforehand. Then he can carefully approach the reptile and nibble on it from behind. But beware, the animals are extremely agile! Smiley is controlled with the joystick in port 2. If he finds himself in a snake's stomach, just press the fire button to start again. Bon appetit and don't spoil your stomach!

177720.overview: A game of "The Big 100" collection and published in the Play on tape Nuova serie - Super Games collection. The aim of the game is simple, it consists of hammering in the heads of moles who dare to poke their heads out of their lairs and into your yard! Just press the right key to give them a reason to relocate.

177721.overview: Smurfette has been kidnapped and is being held atop a platform in Gargamel's castle. The player controls a smurf across the screen and must jump over obstacles, away from spiders, eventually up to smurfette to rescue her. Completing of this task restarts the game with faster moving obstacles and it also takes longer (more scenes) to get to Gargamel's castle.

177722.overview: A Snake\Worm style game developed by Coco Products and published in Game On 1994/07.

177723.overview:
A Snake\Worm style game published in Magic Disk 64 1990/10 where you avoid eating your tail In SNAKE FOR ONE a player has to pick up all the little snakes lolling on the playing field with his big snake. The next field can be reached through an exit that then opens. There is a running hourglass at the top of the screen and a counter below that shows how much time is left to collect the rest of the snakes. 

Below that again is the number of lives that are still available to the player. The color of this number provides information about the tens (white = 1 to 9, cyan = 10 to 19, red = 20 to 29, blue = 30 to 39, yellow = 40 to 49 and black = 50 and more). This is followed by the display of the points achieved and the three-digit display at the bottom right, which, depending on the color, has the following meaning: red = playing field number, cyan = snake speed and black = snake length.

177724.overview: A Worm\Snake variant game with great music and a fantastic look, developed by Twice Effect and published in Game On 1991/12 and in Tutto C64 n.2 (1992/1993).

177725.overview:
With the fast snake you have to try to collect as many objects as possible that appear randomly and only for a short time somewhere on the screen. If you have reached the required number, you can try the next level.

General:
- You should avoid brushing against a building or the wall of the enclosure. The result is the loss of a life.
- The same thing happens if you bite your own tail. So make sure to always leave enough space.
- The snake grows the more objects it wraps around it.
Do not be surprised!
- You can accelerate the snake by pressing the fire button. Certain objects can still be reached in this way before they disappear without a trace.

In the upper and lower corner of the screen there is a display that shows how many lives you can still gamble away and how many parts still have to be collected.

In 2-player mode you can try yourself against a human teammate.
The rules remain the same, but the playing field becomes much smaller. 

Game created by Nordic Bytes and published in Magic Disk 64 1993/06.

177756.overview:
A Pac-Man style game from Peter J. Glaze and published in 1983. The SNAKMAN accumulates 5 points for each green token and 25 points for each red token captured. You may obtain more green and red tokens by capturing all of the green tokens. Whenever red tokens are captured, the four colored gremlins turn white and become vulnerable to capture for a period of approximately six seconds. A sound change during the vulnerability period indicates that the period is almost over. The point value for gremlin capture increases according to the number of gremlins captured during a single vulnerability period, and always shows at the bottom of the play area.
 
The colored gremlins must not touch SNAKMAN otherwise the SNAKMAN is forfeited, and replaced with an available spare SNAKMAN. The number of barrier. available spare SNAKMAN tokens always shows in the game play area. The high score for a game session is always dis- played. From time to time, bonus tokens will appear in the bonus area of the maze. The point value of the token is also shown at the bottom of the play area.
 
The joystick for the keyboard keys) have memory. That is to say that the direction indicated by the position of the joystick is remembered. The SNAKMAN will continue in the same direction when the joystick is in the center position or when no keys are pressed. If you control the SNAKMAN in a direction it cannot go (because of a barrier in the maze). it will continue in its original direction until it can move in the desired direction.
The duration of a vulnerability period can be extended by capturing an additional red token before the end of the period. When a gremlin is captured, it returns to the jail in the center of the play area. It does, however. quickly escape from jail. A technique of "working the jail consists of repeated capture of a gremlin just as it escapes from jail. See if you can figure out how to trap and capture gremlins at will while they are in the jail. Working the jail" can build large scores quickly. The bonus tokens are not presented for capture until tokens in the "U-shaped area of the maze are captured. SNAKMAN can be "parked".

177759.overview:
Snake Pit is a fast-paced game where the player controls a character shaped like a grinning face. The goal is to eat up all the eggs that fill up the single screen field entirely and survive as long as possible to reach the next stage. Also in the field are multiple snakes with a different colour. They cannot escape until you make a hole in their wall by eating the eggs there. Only the red snake is able to move about right away. As soon as the snakes are on the loose they start eating the eggs too and the player's character needs to avoid their heads. Their body also gets longer with each egg they eat and that way they can block the path. There is a strategy to it by keeping the snakes walled in as long as possible while avoiding the red snake. The goal is to eat all the eggs so the second stage starts. It has different gameplay as now the goal is to eat the snakes by biting their tails. The game keeps track of the score and the high score is registered. 
 
Published in Italy as Serpents in Mega Games n.4 (dicembre 1987).

177761.overview: This educational spelling game was released on Valueware - The Educator.

177762.overview: A breakout style game with gaps between the bricks so you can get some great combo shots.

177832.overview: Rare Snooker management game. That's right, you don't play Snooker at all, you manage the career of young snooker players and guide them through to the world championships. There's no other game like this.

177834.overview: Snoopy to the Rescue is a 1 - 2 player side-scrolling arcade game featuring the comic character Snoopy. Snoopy needs to save Woodstock from a castle where he is trapped. A side-scrolling arcade game, the player can move left and right, as well as jump. Gameplay consists of multiple stages, where the goal is to climb to the top left corner of the screen. On each level, there are a number of timers, and the player must stop each timer so that their total equals the number displayed on the top of the screen on each level, otherwise Snoopy dies when he reaches the end of the level. Keys are found on each level, and when the player collects a key, the nearest enemy briefly turns orange and stop moving. The player must run into the enemy at this time to destroy them, or the level becomes unbeatable. Other dangers include water, and if Snoopy falls too far, he dies. Each player starts with 5 lives, and when the lives are lost it's game over.

177835.overview: Released as part of the Minigame Competition 2007 - 1K Category, this winter sport game has you racing to the bottom of the snow hill, but don't hit the trees! The close you get to the bottom the faster the action!

177836.overview: The 2nd and final in the series of detective/problem solving games for kids. Armed with your Snoop-mobile, the snoopNET computer, a wrist-radio, flashlight and pen and paper, you're the detective who must solve the case of Lilly, the missing dolphin. The game requires logical thinking, planning, and note taking as you slowly comb the neighborhood gathering clues and evidence. Once the suspect is properly identified, use the snoopNET computer to accuse and ensure that justice has been served.

177837.overview: Santa Claus is flying across the screen dropping presents. This is a race for two players only to grab as many of those presents as possible. The first player to reach their quota wins the game. Watch out though because there are huge snowballs falling from the screen. If one of those hit you or your opponent, then it will freeze the player for a short period of time. Using the fire button will allow Splidge or his friend to jump.

177838.overview:
A single player snowboarding sports game published in Magic Disk 64 1988/08, and then in Digital Marketing PD #098, and also in 64'er Spielesammlung #6. If you miss a goal, you will not be disqualified, but will be added 20 seconds to your time.

The great thing about 'Snowboard Race' is that you are not alone on the slope, but you are racing against the computer. So be quick if you want to be in the top ten!

Snowboard safe!"

177839.overview: A single player, festive crosshairs-shooter published in Game On 1992/12, and in Tiger-Crew-Disk #09 (1994/12). You are Tom, the last bastion of hope against the Snowmen horde. Your parents were killed by the Abominable Snowman, these are his evil minions. The evil snowmen can't keep a grin for long and will soon show their horrible grimace. Hit them with your icy projectiles! Bonus points for hitting Santa if he has a green pressie.

177840.overview: An Italian language avoid-it style PD game by Luigi Recanatese where you dodge the saucers and avoid the aliens in the tunnels. It was released in 1986.

177841.overview: A football\soccer team management game. Train and trade your players, manage injuries and become the best and most profitable in the league.

177842.overview: A European football\soccer management game where you also get to play the game.

177843.overview: In order to succeed in making your team league and cup champions you must answer questions. You can't select your team but you can train them instead by answering questions. If you get the question correct then they improve, answer wrong and they get worse. To play a game against a team you have to answer questions as well. If they're attacking, get the question right and it's saved. Get it wrong and they score. Likewise if you are attacking, right means you score, wrong and it's saved. You start in Division 4 (League 2 here in 2012) and work your way up to Division 1 (Premiership). You also enter the F.A. Cup (still the same) and League Cup (Carling Cup). The game is just text, no graphics here. There are around 2000 questions in the database.

177844.overview: In Soccer Star you are trying to be the best football manager with the best team. At the beginning you have to start with a team from the bottom division, as you are a new manager. As the seasons go on you can start buying better players and try winning every game so you get promoted to next division; your goal is to win the divisions and the cup. As in the real world of football you have to look after your finances with overheads, spy fees and wages. The game can be saved for later resumption.

177845.overview: A soccer management game by Redwood Design and published by White Panther Software in 1988.

177846.overview: Sokoban is a puzzle video game in which the player pushes crates or boxes around in a warehouse, trying to get them to storage locations.

177861.overview: Star Trek: The Kobayashi Alternative was a Star Trek themed computer software game, designed for the Apple II Plus, Apple IIe, and Apple IIc. The game was also available for the Commodore 64, Macintosh and IBM PC. This text adventure was first published in 1985 by Simon & Schuster. The player assumes the role of Captain James T. Kirk. As Kirk, the player commands the actions of the Enterprise crew, as well as the Enterprise itself. The game was expansive and ambitious, but also very buggy.

178321.overview: You play as Xain, the Soldier of Light, who must visit a number of invaded planets and wipe out the evil hordes that have attacked the human populations. The main bulk of the gameplay is a horizontally scrolling run and gun game, while some stages put you in an horizontal shoot 'em up scenario. You take control of Xain, who can jump or duck to avoid enemies and jump up to higher ledges. Lots of extra weaponry can be collected along the way, although this is lost when one of your five lives is lost. Each time you defeat a planet's boss, you control Xain's spaceship and have to go through a short horizontal shmup level, before selecting your next target planet. The planets Cleemalt Soa, Lagto Soa, Cleedos Soa, Kworal Soa and Guwld Soa are all available for selection immediately. These each have their own settings – Cleedos Soa is desert, Cleemalt Soa is moon-like, Lagto Soa is lush and verdant, Kworal Soa is cold and underwater-like and Guwld Soa is a red-hot-steaming Mars type of place. When you clear all planets (plus their respective shmup sections) you gain access to a final planet which resembles the death star from Star Wars. After that,the game is over and you save the planets from the empire invasion.

178331.overview:
Gone with the Wind (Via Col Vento) is appropriate as for all creatures you face, a single shot is enough! You have five lives to sustain you, the war is nearly over, but you have to keep going and have only your courage by your side as you wander in the endless caves using your survival skills to keep you safe from the pitfalls of nature. This immense clay cave full of burial niches, tunnels, crumbling stairs and terrifying creatures is proof the war has not ended for you. But fate is not completely against you because in the cave, scattered here and there are various types of weapons and some creatures require a certain type of weapon to best destroy. 

Published in Italy under Via Col Vento in  Linguaggio Macchina C64/ZX n.14 (Febbraio 1986) and as L'Errante in Poke n.10 (febbraio 1986).

178391.overview: Three of the key battles of the American War of Independence are recreated here. The British army and American patriots can be played by either human or computer (with 3 skill levels). Each side's level of reinforcements and ammunition can be set on a 5-point scale. The smallest and shortest battle is Bunker Hill, while the Battle of Monmouth is distinguished by harsh weather, and Saratoga requires a different fighting style to the highly regimented one the British unsuccessfully used.

178400.overview: A compilation created in Germany for a specific C64 hardware bundle released. The games used were International Soccer, Colossus Chess and Silicon Syborgs.

178402.overview:
The first Hugo game based on the television show Eleva2ren was originally developed by Thomas Villadsen and Uffe Jakobsen for SilverRock Productions.

Skærmtrolden Hugo was released for the Commodore 64 in 1991, and for the Amiga shortly afterwards. The game took place in a gold mine, which Hugo had to navigate to collect treasure. The game mechanics were simple and a complete game could take less than ten minutes.

178412.overview:
Super Password was a popular game show that ran from 1984-1989, and this game was adapted from that television program. Players give and receive clues to 5 Passwords which, when all are listed on the board, suggest the identity of the person, place, thing, event, phrase, etc., that is the Super Password.

Each game consists of three to four rounds. The first round is worth $100, the second $200, the third $300, and the fourth (if necessary) $400. The first player to win $500 (or more) wins the game. The winner gets to play the Final Round for $10,000. To play the Final Round, the winning player must guess the ten Passwords as each one's initial letter is highlighted at the bottom of the stand. Each word is worth $100, but a special bonus of $10,000 is awarded if all ten are guessed.

178424.overview:
A space text-adventure game of the "Cassette 50" collection and also released in Digital Marketing PD #094.  
 
You have crash landed on Mars, with only 24 hours worth of oxygen remaining. Can you survive?

178452.overview:
A pretty nice vertically scrolling space shooter published in Magic Disk 64 1988/07, and also in Stonysoft #0404.

'Solid I' is a space game with a lot of action, good sound, and above all great graphics that can easily keep up with the graphics of commercially available software! There you will find a lot of enemy spaceships and UFOs who want to make life difficult for you. A total of three spaceships are available to you to complete your mission.

Good luck and happy shooting!

The game was developed by Thomas Koncina & Thorsten Koytka using Chris Yates' Shoot 'em Up Construction Kit.

178453.overview: A puzzle Solitaire game published in Game On 1991/03.

178454.overview: A puzzle game created by Amok Developments and published in Game On 1992/11.

178455.overview: A puzzle game created by Oliver Malms and published in both 64'er 1991/08 and 64'er 1999/01. You must clear the game board by jumping over a stone with a neighboring stone to remove it. The goal is to remove as many stones as possible. Now on Solix, the shape of the score changes in each level and a certain number (bound) of stones must be cleared in each level. There are also special items. Solving the level quickly gives a time bonus,  The game cursor is moved with the joystick in port 2. To skip a levels, press fire and steer up or down for different levels.

178456.overview: Solitaire card game, released as part of the Board Game Challengers compilation.

178585.overview:
Try to make money at the stock market. Invest in stocks when their exchange price is low and when the price rises sell them to make profit.

You have $5000 in cash at the beginning of the game and 10 different securities to choose from.

178818.overview:
This is a compilation of the first three Spy vs. Spy games for the Amstrad CPC, Atari 8-bit, Commodore 64 and ZX Spectrum.

The included games are:

Spy vs. Spy
Spy vs. Spy: The Island Caper
Spy vs. Spy III: Arctic Antics

The disk versions have a menu you select your desired game from. For the tape versions, you simply insert the correct tape or side.

178935.overview: Solo Flight (Enhanced) is an expansion of the game Solo Flight and once again allows you to fly a small plane either for the experience of flying or to deliver mail to various airports in three states, Kansas, Washington and Colorado.The changes to the original was a new look cockpit instrument panel and improved speech.

178939.overview:
...Sonar reports the "whine" of torpedoes running towards you. You kick the destroyer's rudder full-right and order flank speed. As you watch, two torpedoes cross your bow. Sonar returns quicken and you close on the submarine below. Suddenly, bearing to target shifts 180 degrees and the sonar return is instantaneous. THE SUB IS DIRECTLY BELOW! You stab the firing button and watch as 6 depth charges arch into your wake. Several long seconds pass before they explode, sending six domes of white water to the surface, along with bits of the sub that nearly got you. But congratulations are brief as four more subs are lurking out there somewhere, trying to escape into the open ocean. 
 
Sonar search is a fast action strategy game based on anti-submarine warfare. You are the commander of a group of 4 destroyers sent to intercept a pack of 5 enemy submarines. Equipped with sonar gear and depth charges, and aided by submarine sightings from other ships and aircraft you must get directly over a sub to score a hit with your depth charges.

179004.overview: Part of a series of games ending in Magical Formula, published in 1997 featuring Sonny the Snail who works to save his home, Snail Meadow.

179006.overview: In this SEUCK game by Richard Bayliss you blast away at the enemy ships in your crumpet shaped space ship. Space Crumpets is a zany space shoot 'em up for 1 or 2 players. Your crumpets have been fired out into deep space. Its mission, to repair Earth's space satellites in order to restore TV and Radio broadcasting. The aliens don't like the idea, so they attempt to TOAST the crumpets. It's a wacky idea, but that's the game for you :) - CRUMPETS AT THE READY!

179009.overview:
The Sorcerer's Apprentice is an arcade game and text adventure for the Commodore 64.

Once upon a time, many years ago before YOP schemes were invented and the Manpower Services Commission was but a wrinkle in a civil servant's eye, young lads were apprenticed to masters. Now, this is your once-in-a-lifetime chance to become apprenticed to a sorcerer, Unfortunately, the sorcerer has whisked himself away on holiday leaving you in charge of the practice. At first, all goes well but then the mischievous brooms decided to flood your reservoir.

In the arcade component, two brooms carry buckets of water from the left side of the screen to the right. The sorcerer must try to run into them, preventing them from reaching the right of the screen, where the brooms pour their water into the reservoir. Whenever a broom reaches the right, the water level rises. If a broom is intercepted, it immediately rushes back to the left of the screen to pick up more water. At the same time other creatures try to steal bricks from the reservoir, making it require less water to cause a flood. The player is armed with a magic wand which can be used up to 3 times per game to temporarily freeze the brooms. The goal is to prevent enough brooms from reaching their goal to reach skill level 2, to acquire a passcode for the text adventure.

179010.overview:
Dark and foreboding against the early dawn, Vygors castle stands atop the mountain. A village huddles against the sheer cliff face, seeking safety in its ancient stone. But, its only release can come through me. I, Sanec, son of the great wizard Osyth, whose scrolls and orb of power were stolen by the evil sorcerer Vygor. Now I must recover these before the moon of three days hence or the forces of evil will destroy the orb, and loose the Satanic hordes upon this Earth. 

This was a text adventure written as a sample game of "AdventureWriter"

179011.overview: Sorry! is a licensed computer implementation of the Parker Brothers board game. Four players take turns drawing cards from a stack, in an attempt to be the first player to move their four pieces from the starting location around the board, and back to the home location. Initially, a player must draw a 1 or a 2 to move their piece out of the starting location. Sliding pieces allow the player to move an extra distance, and if two pieces land on the same location, the original occupying piece is sent back to their home to restart their journey. The player can set any number of the 4 players to be controlled by the computer. Other unique cards include the seven, whose moves can be divided between multiple players, and the four, which allows the player to move backwards. There is also the "Sorry" card, which allows the player to switch position with an opponent piece.

179013.overview: The sequel to SOS Terrorists aka Terrorist released by CBM and Virgin\Aakosoft respectively. It is a multi-genre action\strategy\shooter. You control an anti-terrorist squad with access to multiple forms of vehicle and weaponry to stop the terrorists from overrunning a randomly generated city location with all the tools at your disposal.

179014.overview: Originally a fan work but picked up and published commercially in 64'er 1993/12 with very good sound, good graphics and 1351 mouse support. Mapping recommended for the deep dungeons. A role-playing game where the player selects adventurers and descend into the depths of the dungeon. The gameplay is reminiscent of the 3D dungeon crawl type of role-playing games popularized by Dungeon Master, Wizardry and The Bard's Tale.

179104.overview: A Space Invaders style shooter Published by the Norway Game Maker Association.

179108.overview:
A vertically scrolling space shooter made with SEUCK and created by David Carter. Fly over enemy bases along the pipes\corridors there are enemy fire centers which emit shots in continuous sequence and in all directions, with trajectories that include diagonal. Avoid the shots, blow up as many foes as possible. Game can be played by 2 simultaneous players, but new solutions bring new problems and they sometimes come in continuous succession. Good luck!

Published in Italy as Space Trooper in Logica 2000 n.89 (1989).

179110.overview: Sir Tommy: A Game of Old Patience is a solitaire/patience card game  for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Barbara H. Schulak and published by Softdisk Publishing, Inc. in the North American based disk magazine Loadstar. It was in Loadstar #51.

179111.overview:
Space Battle Deluxe is a simple strategy game for up to four players (Lords) and optionally a computer opponent "Deep Jones", who is, however, not the brightest. Each player commands a fleet of spaceships and tries to conquer a randomly calculated galaxy, which on many planets is already inhabited by neutral peoples (natives). At the beginning each participant chooses his home world. The first player then enters his commands ("from which planet to which fly xx spaceships) invisibly. In the status window he can then see his worlds with an overview of production rate per year and the stock of ships. The game ends after a given number of game years (10 - 999). The a report is created to find the winner. 
 
This game is the forerunner to Advanced Space Battle.

179112.overview: A one or two player space shooter from Celestial Software and published in 1983.

179113.overview: Released as part of "War Games" game pack. Reverse Missile command. Bomb the cities and avoid the shots from the cities.

179114.overview:
In this type-in BASIC game from Compute! magazine, the player takes control of a ship beset by an unfortunate set of circumstances. Not only is it trapped in a series of caverns (presumably in space), it's also given a less-than-welcoming reception by the local residents - a rather unfriendly bunch of aliens. In each room, four of them will try to chase down your ship, and you'll only have your forward-firing gun to get you by. Once the room is cleared of aliens, it's on to the next one; the rooms are grouped into levels, each with more rooms than the last. Between levels, you will be treated to a bonus round, which lets you take revenge on your pursuers: the aliens are now stationary, and you will have to hunt down as many as you can before time runs out. In each session, the game keeps track of the three highest scores.

Published in COMPUTE! 1985/03 (Issue #58).

179115.overview: Space Arena is a two player only one on one combat game similar to a lot of those old tank vs tank games except you're in  space ships. It was published in: COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1986/01 (Issue #31), Best of COMPUTE! & Gazette, Stonysoft #0040, Stonysoft #0519.

179116.overview: An unpublished dueling game for 2 player Only simultaneous play apparently based on or related to Space Combat that was released by Caesar Software except that Walt Harned added to Bryan Files' original code from that game.

179117.overview: This is a multigenre game that starts you off as an Indiana Jones lookalike, and progresses into two SHMUP levels and an avoid-the-falling-blocks one.

179123.overview: A SEUCK based, vertically scrolling space shooter where you command your Tie-Fighter-like craft in deepest space and over giant space stations shooting all the baddies before they get you.

179125.overview: Published in both Magic Disk 64 1988/05, and in Digital Marketing PD #034, Space Fight is a typical vertically scrolling shooting game. With Space Fight you can confidently set your joystick to 'AUTOFIRE' and start the hopeless fight against the space opponents. But watch out! Only a very limited number of spaceships are available to you.

179195.overview:
Test your downhill skiing skills on four different pistes, one of which is randomly generated every time you load the game! You might make it across the finishing line after going down Rocky Ridge, but have you got have what it takes to finish Bear Mountain? Ski season is over, the bears are starting to wake up, and collecting the piste flags so they can be reused next year will earn you bonus points.

Connect your joystick to port 2. Move the joystick up/down on the title screen to select a course, and press fire to start. Look out for those bears!

Credits:
Programming by Andreas Gustafsson
Graphics and sound by Vanja Utne

179259.overview: An Italian Dueling game for 2 player simultanous play. Released in 1989 by Systems Editoriale s.r.l. and created by Ivan Del Duca.

179264.overview: A pretty well done crosshairs shooter with faux vector line graphics. Space Gunner is an exciting video arcade-type game for the Commodore-64 with the object being to defend the planet Namcap against the fleet of the Warlords of Zorlon. The screen shows the display from inside the cockpit of an attack ship. The joystick is used to aim the gunsight and fire to destroy the approaching Zorlons. The control panel at the bottom of the screen gives continuous readouts of both fuel and scores. As the player's ship absorbs energy from exploding Zorlon ships, the fuel count rises. The level of difficulty increases and the game progresses.

179269.overview:
Created by Mercer Mayer and originally released in 1985 by Mindscape, re-released as "Subtraction With the Tink Tonks" by Thunder Mountain. Education-Ages 4-8. Designed and developed by Angelsoft. In this program, children strengthen their math skills by solving basic subtraction problems in the context of five highly motivating educational activities. Each activity offers multiple levels of difficulty to match or challenge a child's skill.

Educational Benefits helps children:
• Strengthen mathematical skills
• Understand principles of earning and spending
• Develop critical thinking skills
• Improve memory and concentration 
 

Features
• Challenging for ages 4 to 8
Five multilevel educational activities Bold, high-resolution graphics
• Clear, on-screen instructions
• Lively animation
• Original music throughout

179305.overview: A racing game where the goal is to stay on the track without crashing into the walls.

179384.overview:
In the distant future, the earth will be attacked by alien spaceships whose aim is to steal natural resources. As the most experienced pilot, you have been chosen to destroy the alien headquarters. To do this, you have to fight your way through all the levels of defense. There are 3 spaceships available for each task, whereby there are extra ships for every level achieved. Should you survive all nine levels, you will return to earth as a hero. 

Released in the following:

•   Magic Disk 64 1988/03
•   Digital Marketing PD #072.

179385.overview: A fun educational math game published by Green Valley Publishing, Inc. Under their ShareData label and part of the "Let's Count" collection. Let's Count helps young children of 4 years and above with early numerical skills for the numbers 0 to 9. Space Hopper gives practice in discriminating whether there are more, less or equal quantities of two objects. Your child's task is to drive the terratruck and load up the space hopper from the space store.

179386.overview: This conversion of Space Invaders stays very true to the original despite being written in BASIC. Game play is exactly the same with the player in control of a tank at the bottom of the screen firing at advancing aliens. The aliens fire back and the player can take cover behind bunkers. The bunkers give way a little bit easier than in the arcade version due to fewer pixels. The sound also tries to stay true to the original with the ever increasing speed of the beat when the aliens draw nearer. Obviously the Commodore PET version does not feature any colour in its graphics. The Commodore 64 version does, but the aliens don't change color as they draw nearer. part of "Arcade Games I" pack.

179388.overview: Space Journey, written in conjunction with leading experts in the field of education, is a program designed to motivate children to practice and improve percent skills. Children are given two minutes either to intercept meteors or to land on planets by successfully solving percent problems. The challenge is to solve problems correctly or to be lost in space. 3 levels of difficulty offer hours of variety and motivating practice on percent, the math skill that most children find most difficult.

179389.overview:
A vertically scrolling space shooter. Sector 93D in the year 2073, the Alpha-Pluto base was attacked. The defense forces did not manage to disperse the mass attack of the Rovolians. Fortunately, a group of inhabitants of the colony managed to escape the clutches of the aliens and hid in the radioactive deposits, enclosed within leaden walls to resist until reinforcements can arrive. Unfortunately, as you know, a place like this is not very healthy, and that is why you have volunteered to go with your Space Knight fighter to help them. As soon as you fly over the base you will realize that the enemy has not been idle, but has taken over the anti-aircraft systems to attack you from your own base! Waves of his shuttles appear from all over to thwart you, you will you be able to withstand the various waves unharmed?!
 
Published in Italy as Future Bomber and published in Hit Parade C64 n.42 (Febbraio 1990) and in New Special PlayGames n.26 (dicembre 1989).

179392.overview: Very much like Invadagame, this was a game that could load into memory while the actual game you purchased was loading. Since game loading on the C64, especially for those using cassette tape based games, was extremely slow. This gave you something fun to do while your purchased game prepared to be played. Gamebase has this as unpublished, but it was definitely published just not as it's own game. Always a bridesmaid, never the bride. The differences between this and Invadagame are small and mostly cosmetic but are there, nonetheless.

179393.overview:
A Galaga\Galaxian style single screen shooter where you try to destroy the aliens that move in waves. You are the last survivor of the lunar base GERXI 21 and now the hordes of aliens are attacking! Your task is to repel them for as long as possible. Your weapon is a ground-to-air laser cannon with which you have to hit as many enemies as you can while being careful not to be hit by one of them, as you would lose a life. If you successfully complete the game you will need to reload to play again. 

Published in Italy as Invasori in both Hit Parade C64 n.67 (Maggio 1992) and in Special Program n.84 (febbraio 1992).

179394.overview: A two-player-only game for simultaneous shoot'em up action for you and a friend. Grab your mate and take down the baddies before they get to your shield generators and attack your base!

179395.overview: Mental maths meets Lunar Lander. Three difficulty levels to chose from. And 5 problem sets including Addition, subtraction, Multiplication, Division or Random questions from the other groups.

179397.overview: A two player only simultaneous play game, but not a cooperative game. The two players compete to get 10 points first. Points are obtained by having a rendezvous, which is only possible if landed or crashed.

179400.overview:
Space Dodge is a simple game developed in BASIC by Gary Wilson. It was published as a type-in by Fontana Paperbacks in 1984 in the book "Giant Book of Games for Your Commodore 64."

You play the spaceship on top of the screen, your goal is to avoid all the asteroids coming up the screen by pressing J (left) and K (right) on the keyboard.

179401.overview:
Space Rox is a 1-player avoid it game for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Jason Kelk and Tomas Danko of Bigtime Software, and released into the public domain in 1995.

 Fly through space and avoid the space rox, or they will take you out!

179402.overview: A game of the "Cassette 50" collection. You must find a planet capable of supporting life. If you collide with a planet you lose. If you fly next to a planet you can take on fuel and check to see if this is the planet you have been searching for.

179403.overview: A game of the "Casette 50" collection where you must enter several rooms in the base in search of your space-craft which has been stolen by the robot inhabitants of the planet. Unfortunately the robots will electrify you if they manage to capture you! The robots are planning to attack earth. You must escape to give a warning to Earth's defenses. If you fail the Earth is DOOMED!

179429.overview: An educational game focused on maths that was part of "Let's Count" collection. Let's Count helps young children of 4 years and above with early numerical skills for the numbers 0 to 9. Space Stations gives experience in matching number quantities to their number symbols. Your child is captain of the space rocket which is going to put a space station on a distant planet. Your child has to pick the planet that matches the number of solar panels on his/her rocket. When all the space stations are sending out signals strange forces take over the movement of the planets.

179430.overview:
An early version of Hero of the Golden Talisman, which is quite a bit different, featuring different music, screens, enemies and a rather bizarre swimming animation! It was leaked to the scene and has been floating around under a number of different pseudonyms including "Labyrinth" and "Progfine" at one point.
 
Published in Italy as Minaccia al Mondo in Logica 2000 n.18 (Marzo 1986).

179432.overview: A frustratingly challenging scrolling screen platformer published in Game On 1992/11.

179435.overview: A Centipede style shooter where the goal is to stop the Space Train before it gets down to you. Blast it!

179462.overview:
In this 2D action game player assumes the role of a maintenance engineer, who was deployed by mistake on the desolate planet on the outer rim of the universe. It is the year 2040 A.D. and humanity is turning the planets and moons into a series of huge hydroponic greenhouses. Because the protagonist is out of money, his only goal is to pay his way home by taking the worst job in the galaxy, enlisting himself into the ranks of the Space Vegetable Corps. Players move the protagonist wearing a spacesuit on the moon surface, protecting the vegetables growing in domes, shooting the alien forms, and collecting certain vegetables to reach a quota set for a day on a moon. There are three moons (Phobos, Diemos and Riscos) to complete. The characters wears a jetpack that allows him to fly. Flying aliens sometimes want to steal a dome. These aliens have to be eliminated, but sometimes the dome breaks if the creature is killed too high above the surface. Certain creatures release oxygen after dying, and it can be collected to refill the spacesuit's reserve. Vegetables grow inside the dome in a cyclical manner and they need to be collected when they have a sufficient height. When the quota is reached, another day with a new quota begins until the character is transferred to the next moon. When all domes with vegetables are destroyed or when the oxygen is exhausted, the game is over. Top 10 galactic gardeners are stored in hi-scores table. 
 
Was released by MicroValue as part of the Mega Collection.

179464.overview:
Published in Ahoy! 1985/10 (Issue #22). Gravinauts (aka Space Walk in the Caesar Software release) requires you to fight for survival in the hostile environment of the planet Arkion. n the world of Arkion, Survival is a tough business. Because the surface of the planet is covered by a deadly acidic ocean, the inhabitants must remain ontinuously in the air, supported by rocket backpacks. To stay up, they engage in a never-ending war for fuel. The loser is doomed to a very short lifespan. 

The Gravinauts, as they are called by the colonies of the Milky Way, battle each other by trying to reach a higher vantage point in the air than their opponents and smashing into them, destabilizing their gyros and causing their backpacks to explode. 

Because the fuel tanks stored higher up in the atmosphere are more closely guarded, they are entrusted with greater fuel supplies. They are therefore more important than the ones resting on the lower "ice glaciers," which are huge bodies of frozen chemicals floating in the air above the ocean. 
The purpose of the game is to take fuel off the glaciers.

179466.overview:
Published in Magic Disk 64 1988/10, Digital Marketing PD #082. A horizontally scrolling space shooter. Much like a poor man's Delta. It goes on forever.

Unfortunately, after the great and last intergalactic battle, which ended with no clear winner and only losers, the universe fell into a chaotic and terrifying situation. In fact, gangs of outlaws and the possessed roam through the air and underground spaces where they sow panic and terror, plundering defenseless citizens and taking wealth and goods that could have been in the marketplace. They were created, in the past, to defend themselves form these evil surveillance teams that flew over the planet. Take them out and as you progress through your career you will get improvements for your ship which will make things a bit easier. When you have defeated all the enemies you will be crowned as Space Warrior!

179467.overview: A space themed board game for 2 head-to-head players.

179468.overview:
A racing game for 1 or 2 players published in 64'er Sonderheft 61. In the vast universe, far from any imagination, lies the wall of time. Yes, any one of us can fall into one of the innumerable dimensional holes and, in order to return from the other side of the universe, has to compete in the big race in the Space Ball. 
 
It was late in the evening and there was nothing sensible on the television (although he had a front row seat). So Walter Hombert put down his diet biscuits and decided to switch off the boob tube. Slowly, somewhat disappointed by what the program makers had offered him today, he switched himself out of his bulky television armchair, which, due to its unfavorable construction, had not even allowed him a well-earned television sleep. With weary steps he shuffled to the light switch to tell his living room by depriving himself of the light that this was finally the end of it - he didn't believe his senses, his hand groped in emptiness. Walter, a normally stressed person, lost his balance almost immediately. But the wall, as usual, did not stop his fall: he fell right through it. Into the great, dark nothingness. When Walter regains consciousness, he notices that everything around him has changed. Slight nausea galls his general condition, and he soon knows the reason. A constant up and down movement, each followed by a melodic pop: A water bed? What happened?

Walter remembers reading about dimension holes in a paper by Anton Einfels. But can you believe it? Just now, before he went to bed, he fell into one of them. And much worse: According to Professor Einfels' theory, the big spaceball race is imminent. Somewhere in our real world, a C64 owner loads the game LOAD "SPACEBALL II", 8 and starts with RUN. With this, he activates Walter's spaceball and perhaps wakes him up from his nightmare.

179469.overview:
The prevalence of the once highly cultured human race in the universe has been broken for centuries. the extruders, a highly intelligent, but completely unfeeling, breed of lizard, spread more and more in the outskirts of the worlds.

But hope is now germinating in the slave camps of the extrudian empire: one tells of a spacefighter in a space cruiser eagle mk 3, who wants to search the blue gene on the planet intro for the salvation of humanity.

Against this backdrop, they now appear as commander of the eagle mk3 in scene.

You're in the atmosphere of the peaceful oxygen world Ilfus on the edge of the Pegus system. Your ship is equipped only with the most-needed: take-off device and buglaser of the class 4.

You have to abandon your ship for the dangerous mission. Since your capital is only 100 cr (credits), you should first get money.

The most convenient method is by catching animals.
Published in Magic Disk 64 1990/03.

179470.overview: A don't-touch-the-walls maze game published as a game of "The Big 100" collection.

179474.overview:
The game was originally created with GAC in 1986 and published by Trom (Tony Rome) Software. In 1993, it was re-released in a new version. 
 
You, an international superspy, are forced to bail out of your plane when the pilot of another plane shoots your pilot. And as soon as your parachute reaches the ground the killer is coming for you. Packed with excitement and adventure, see if you can retrieve the treasure and make it safely back to Britain.

179476.overview: Published in Commodore Zone Issue #09 (January/February/March 1997). SEUCK driving game for 1-2 players. Made in 1994 by Ryan Weekes with some cracking music by Thomas Mogensen.

179477.overview: It's the 21st century in America. Technology has improved by leaps and bounds, and now (most) people live in peace. But in a small town somewhere, a vicious terrorist group known as Zapper is terrorizing small towns and kidnapping innocent people so that they can build a secret weapon. And, as it turns out, the family and friends of someone code-named "Super Joe" just so happened to be one of the innocents caught! Now Super Joe's hungry for revenge. Can Super Joe and his armored car destroy the Zapper organization and save his town from utter destruction in time? The Speed Rumbler is a action game where the player races against the clock in an armored car piloted by Super Joe, destroying other cars and saving captives along the way. Super Joe's car is armed with a gun that he can use to shoot down enemy cars, but the enemy cars have a few tricks up their sleeve, so Super Joe should always be on guard. As the player progresses through the game's six stages, Super Joe can be given a boost by saving captives, who then award him with bonus points, increased fire power, or speed-ups. If Super Joe's car is destroyed, he can continue the fight on foot with his rifle. But unfortunately, Super Joe is not as powerful as his car - one hit and he's history. Super Joe has 24 "hours" to destroy Zapper. The game is over when Super Joe runs out of lives or time - or if he successfully completes his mission.

179478.overview: Speed Runner is a 'Light Cycle' game for two human players. The game consist of 10 duels. Each player drives around the board leaving a solid trail behind. The collision with the trail or the board edge means a loss of the duel. The winner of more duels wins the game.

179479.overview: The game that helps you learn to read more quickly but retain what you've read.

179481.overview:
Like the original "Speed Zone", this is a vertically scrolling shoot'em up with a classic style.

The player, who flies a latest-generation spacecraft, must destroy all the alien hordes who want to destroy the space federation. The spaceship has a shield with a limited amount of energy. This energy protects the ship from the alien craft's shots. When the energy shield has reached its limit, the player loses one of three lives.

179493.overview:
A cross between Pong and air-hockey, a 2-player only head to head game. In a small arena with molybdenum walls, two players with nerves of steel will have to volley with a titanium sphere at constant acceleration using to gravito-magnetic repulsors that will be able to move in a limited area of the playing field. The aim being not only to protect one's own goal,  but to score the greatest number of goals on your opponent. Since the sphere will move faster and faster and with sometimes unpredictable direction, be very careful not to score on your own self!

Published in Italy as Old Game in both Hit Parade C64 n.19 (Gennaio 1988) and in Special Program n.37 (novembre 1987).

179494.overview: Tron Light Cycles for 2 simultaneous players.

179496.overview: An overhead view racing game published in Game On 1989/01, and in Digital Marketing PD #114.

179506.overview: A good platformer, remarkable graphically, lively, quite nice in the controls and of moderate thickness. A little tenacious but you get used to it. Set in the "micro world" of insects, snails and other nice crap, who will return to this habitat for the equally good and colorful "Sonny the Snail" and "Bobix" (almost all clone between them, conceptually ..). Extraordinary visual impact, fluid scroll and very pleasant to play.

179531.overview: An educational spelling game created by Dean Hodgson for Pyramid Software, released in 1983. There are 168 lessons in total to increase your knowledge with the ability to review problem lessons and master and overcome spelling weaknesses.

179538.overview: Quickly match 3 in a row to remove them from the playing field and rack up a big score. Published in Game On 1994/05 / a.k.a. "Spiranza"

179540.overview: Published in 64'er 1995/12, this is a logic game where the sphere you control can push certain types of blocks with the goal of getting all the dots on the field. Choose which blocks to shift to allow you to get all of them. Other types of blocks can give boosts to help you survive.

179542.overview: This is VG Vox's final submission for the compo. This is a fun vertical scrolling Denarius inspired SEUCK creation. Your mission is to fly your Star MIG fighter past several alien bases, and make a good mess out of them. Then try to reach your home port. You are going to be having a real tough fight on your hands - so you'd better have that FIRE BUTTON handy and an appetite for intergalactic destruction.

179705.overview:
A cross-hair shooter published in the book "Winning Games on the Commodore 64".

Also released commercially in Germany by Oldi-Soft.

179707.overview: In this game from AVL and released in 1983, you are a spider and your web it full of juicy flies. You have one minute to eat as many as you can. Watch out for low-flying bees, though, especially since they often will try to drop things on you. At higher levels some flies shoot back!

179734.overview: An outstanding arcade-style game in the vein of Amidar. Only the skillful can evade the random power spikes and escape the grid. Published in COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1983/12 (Issue #6), COMPUTE!'s Second Book of Commodore 64,Your Commodore 1986/02, Digital Marketing PD #082, as well as Your Commodore 1986/02.

180003.overview: A tough game, snow joke. Guide Splidge left & right, collecting falling presents. But avoid collision with those biblets that just want to cover you in snow. Crazy game. Sort of fun in some kind of way.

180004.overview: Splitter is a puzzle game. The player has to complete the picture using randomly selected pieces in a given amount of time. However all the pieces are not visible at once - the game proposes one piece but the player can rotate it using up and down arrow keys selecting a different one to be placed. From the regular puzzle it is distinguished by the fact that each piece has to be slid into its place on the final picture. If it is placed wrong, then the piece goes back to the pool of pieces. But there is also a penalty - a misplaced piece activates a bomb explosion that removes, in a horizontal or vertical line from it, several pieces that have been already correctly placed. The player has to be also aware if placing the pieces do not block others to be slid in. If such thing happens, the only possibility is to misplace a piece and wait for the explosion to remove the blocking pieces.

180005.overview: A timed puzzle game by Harald Sprung and published in Game On 1995/03.

180007.overview:
It's 20 minutes to midnight on Halloween. On a bet you're about to explore the neighborhood's haunted house. You have 20 minutes to escape before Dracula comes to kill you.

This game is a conversion of the game Haunted House published in 1979 by Radio Shack. The puzzles are more or less the same but the map is different and the time limit with Dracula has been added.

180008.overview: Use your spork to stab roaming baddies. Plays like crap with a gamepad through emulation. Nice music though. Would be better off with actual hardware and a joystick, or a PC joystick instead of a pad.  Nice concept, almost sort of like a Whack-a-Mole variant. Published in GO64! 2005/07, and in GO64! 2005/10.

180034.overview:
Show jumping, also known as "stadium jumping", "open jumping", or simply "jumping", is a part of a group of English riding equestrian events that also includes dressage, eventing, hunters, and equitation. Jumping classes are commonly seen at horse shows throughout the world, including the Olympics.  
Published in Golden Disk 64 #04 (1989).

180035.overview:
A horizontally scrolling shooter. Accounted as more of a preview of a game than a full release by many.From polar base Antaeus 4 to Pulus III Starfleet Command: "It is requested with absolute priority to send rescue forces to counterattack against unidentified alien objects intending to take over our home base. We recommend sending sub-photonic helix with magnetic shields equipped with sophisticated laser weapons. We recommend the use of a highly qualified pilot capable of withstanding incessant enemy attack along all the 250 kilometers of the border. Urgency: ABSOLUTE PRIORITY. Alert Status: RED!

Published in Italy as Intercept in both Hit Parade C64 n.22 (Aprile 1988) and Special Program n.36 (ottobre 1987).

180036.overview: Avoid the ghosts in the one to four player platforming game by Data Becker GmbH, released in 1984. A unique feature of this game is the ability to set difficulty by player to allow a fair handicap by skill level.

180065.overview: A Spy Hunter "sequel" as implemented with SEUCK and made by TCE.

180081.overview: Dr. Xavier Tortion (aka Dr. X), jewel thief and smuggler extraordinaire, is on the loose; intelligence reports he is somewhere in North America along with numerous jewels he's stolen. Your job will be to find the jewels and locate Dr. X! Adventures in North America is an educational adventure game which is similar to the Carmen Sandiego series of games. In the game you will need to travel to various North American locations to search for clues; some clues have been left behind by friendly agents and indicate where jewels are located. Sometimes you will come across an informant; if bribed with money or jewels, you will receive a clue as to Dr. X's where about. When you think you have enough clues, you can guess where Dr. X is hiding; you only get three guesses though, so if you keep guessing wrong the game will end. If you are successful in your mission, you are given an efficiency rating; the fewer turns you can locate Dr. X in and the more jewels recovered, the better your score will be.

180082.overview: Minigame Competition 2009 - 2K Category. Move your square around the pit, collecting small white squares, but watch out for those other squares that don't match your colour.

180083.overview: Square Pairs is a matching game of memory and concentration. Choose two numbers from a set of squares on the computer screen to uncover hidden words. Your goal is to find the squares that match. A match con be any two things that go together, such as a horse and carriage or day and night. If the words don't match they are re-covered. Choose again, and try to remember where the words are.

180084.overview: Guide your white square around the inner pit, collect those small white squares to boost up your score, but watch out for the blue, red, green and yellow squares, which can cause you to lose lives. Once lives are all gone, the game is over.

180087.overview:
A stimulating super Space Shuttle shooter. The game seems heavily influenced by the arcade classic, Astro Blaster. The Omega 4 Square Sphere space ship, built with new and exotic scientific techniques, was destined for the exploration of the newly discovered Zone 8, being particularly feared due to the alien forces that populate it. But an unexpected threat is headed for the eastern United States and the ship is the only one that can intervene in time! Waves of meteorites that intend to rain down on the earth and create an extinction event. Destroy all the meteorites, you are the only hope for the world. 

Published in Italy as New York Attack, shortened to Attak in Poke n.13 (maggio 1986).

180091.overview: A Brain\Logical game for one player, created by Michael Grüber and published in 1991 and also in C64 Starlight #06.

180092.overview: A miscellaneous strategy game published in 64'er 1997/08. Thinking game a la "connect four" for two people.

180093.overview: Square-Scape is a Brain\Logic Puzzle game developed by Paul and Mark Kubiszyn and published under their own label (M&P Software) in 1994. Square-Scape is a totally new type of puzzle game, in which the sole aim is to reach the exit on each level. This would be an easy task, if you did not have a Move counter that allowed only a certain number of Moves in which to complete each level. You take control of the yellow and red striped square, using a joystick in port 2. You may Hove in any of the four directions, up, down, left, right, only if the adjacent square is free. At this point you lose one move. On most levels a token depicted by a 'T' is shown. By touching this, the exit will either appear or Move this may help or hinder your progress.

180094.overview: One or two player squash ball! Released in the UK as part of the Golden Oldies compilation.

180096.overview: In part one you escape the squeaky roundabout and make your way deep into the universe. In part 2 you make your way from the space station and back to the roundabout with the solution that everyone needs and back to the green. If you dig that adventure and find the green you may find a treasure almost as nice as the adventure you had along the way.

180097.overview: An action game created by Mania-Soft and released in 1986. A 3-D version of Pong seen from the perspective of the pong players. You control a black paddle on the far wall.
