195046.overview: Suicide Run is a side scrolling shooter similar to Moon Patrol developed by David W. Light and published by Argus Specialist Publications Ltd. as a type-in program in Your Commodore 1987/07.

195056.overview: A full re-write of a game with AdventureWriter that was originally published in PC Computer Games. After a plane crash investigate a mysterious light before being rescued.

195863.overview: A mad scientist is terrorizing the village of St. Jives and a spell must be cast to stop him taking over. Originally released in 1988 by Dorothy Millard, later published in the UK by Atlas Adventure Software in 1990.

195886.overview:
A SEUCK based shooter for 1 or 2 players, including simultaneous cooperative play. Released in Digital Marketing PD #092, released as Super Ball by Editions Fermont in Italy in Go Games n.43 (maggio 1989).  
 
With this beautiful arcade style game you can display your ability to control the Super Ball which you use to destroy the various asteroids and the many enemies that you will find along your path.

196044.overview: You are performing Skeet shooting in the Alps. Ten clay disk-shaped pigeons are flying from bottom to the top in different angular directions one after another. When clay disk starts to fly, the aim of your shotgun is in bottom position. You should mark the flying clay disk with the aim and shoot it. Shoot as much clay disks as you can. Published in Commodore 64 Club #01 [Italian Release].

196470.overview: Published on Loadstar #63, Sentinel is a strategy game dealing with a war in space. You are a captain of a vessel not completely unlike USS Enterprise. Turn on the red alert and win the battle for us, for the humanity is depending on you!

196496.overview:
Space Pirates is an arcade action game written in Basic and published in 64'er 1993/07, a German C64 magazine 64'er as a type-in game. You're controlling a space ship in a middle of a mine field and your job is to avoid touching anything on screen. 

One curious choice in game design is the reversed controls; as the ship is traveling downwards, pulling your joystick left takes the ship right and vice versa.

196608.overview:
Another re-skinned game of the well-received Showdown for the Commodore 64. They took good care to make it ready for the Holiday season with amazing graphics. In the game, you play a Santa out to win a fierce gun duel. The first one to outwit and knock down the opponent 5 times is the winner of the duel. It can be played by 1 or 2 players. 
 
Giddy-up and get ready to fight! 
 
Each canon can carry 5 snowballs. You reload by manually replacing the snowballs with a click of the joystick button, or you can pick up snowball packs from the ground. But beware! If your opponent catches you out of the safety of the snowmen, then you might get knocked down!

Explosive crates appear around the play area. They explode when shot, so better stay away from them if you value you life, cowboy!

The game was initially a purchase only digital release, it was however, made free on December 4, 2021.

196920.overview:
Worm! is rather original take on the snake variant in which you must eat all the mushrooms and then find the exit to get to the next level while avoiding or shooting the Grim Reapers roaming around the maze. In order to shoot you must first collect bullets that can be found around the maze. 

As in all Snake variants, every time you eat a mushroom your body gets longer, making it increasingly difficult to avoid Mr Reaper.

Published in Italy as Serpentone in Special Program n.84 (febbraio 1992) and in Hit Parade C64 n.67 (Maggio 1992).

197026.overview: Sonar is a first-person rail shooter published in a spanish magazine "Lenguaje Maquina" in which you're apparently defending a lunar base from continuous attacks of the unknown enemy.

197310.overview:
Storm-Tamer: The Numehra Saga is a text based RPG for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Jon Mattson and published in Loadstar #78. Written with Jon's QuestWriter program (from Loadstar #76) this huge text adventure teleports you to a land that never was, but will always be.  
 
Gazing out over the nearly empty tavern, you idly wipe an ale mug with a cloth and whistle tunelessly. AS you set it down at the end of a long, neat row, a humorless smile flickers across your lips. You must have the cleanest, shiniest mugs on the coast...
Business has been dismal lately. The weather has been wreaking havoc With Village commerce in general. Weather? Well, that's a tame word for it. Hurricane winds, battering tidal waves and insidious floods hardly qualify as mere weather. A terrible thing to have happened to an honest innkeeper.
You frown and chastise yourself: at least you have a roof over your head, and a stout one at that. Many of the villagers have been forced to desert their homes or flee from homes deserting them! What's worse, those that have journeyed up the coast return with stories of even worse conditions. 'Tis indeed a grim time.

Your musings are interrupted by the clatter of the door being forced open against the wind. An old man pauses for a moment on the threshold, as if deciding belatedly how best to make an entrance. Rain runs in rivulets off his floppy hat and down his dark gray robe, forming little pools around his feet. 
 
With a decisive lurch forward, he steps up to the bar and faces you, his eyebrows knitting together as he studies your face. "I would have words with the owner of this establishment." The words seem to echo up from a grumbling pit. "Then, it is I you seek." You bow your head deferentially. Long years of dealing with strangers have taught you that those of rank do not always appear in noble guise, and this one has an odd feel about him.
"Impossible." He gazes at you like a liar, then raises one eyebrow. How foolish of me. Your father. It is your father I want." "Ah, It is your turn to look dubious. "Well then, my friend, you are a good deal too late. My father died. Well on nine years ago, пон." But your curiosity is piqued: your father was a mage of some note and an adventurer before retiring to the inn. Anyone looking for him could prove very interesting, indeed... 

"Dead?" He looks thoughtful. "Has it been so long?" A sigh and then he sits down on a stool beside you. "Well, then, I guess it has. Have my deepest sympathies... A drink is sorry consolation, but you pass him one nonetheless" It's all right. That was a long time ago. But perhaps I can help you...?"
"Yes, breaking out of his reverie, he eyes you long and steadily. Perhaps you can. It is actually an object I seek - something that was in your father's possession.

197334.overview: Not to be confused with the Amiga/Atari ST game of the same name, this game is a vertically scrolling shooter for 1-2 players (co-op) developed by Weird Scientists using SEUCK. It was published in Magic Disk 64 1988/09 and in Italy as Battle X in Byte Games n.24 (ottobre 1988).

197372.overview:
A German Star Trek themed text and graphic adventure game, in English the title is Star Trek: Escape to Paradise. Starbase II really is one of the most awkward places in the galaxy. Not because of the food or the prices, rather the administration has suffered from a permanent shortage of staff since the galactic crisis of 2273. The administration came up with an ugly method to kidnap unsuspecting travelers who were in the orbit of Starbase II or its planet Regula IV and then use certain means to oblige them to do good service.

No one has ever heard of a victim again.

Your adventure on Starbase II begins as a "person without a memory".

To escape, you first have to find a way to get to Starbase III. With a lot of luck and a good plan, you can then hijack an interstellar spaceship and escape the slavery.

Published with Drachental in the Abenteuer-Paket 2 game pak.

197493.overview: Sherlock Holmes: His Most Difficult Case is a fanmade text adventure starring the popular sleuth created by Sir Arthur Conan Doyle. It was developed by Andrew Williams, and was released in 2001 for the Commodore 64 Crap Game Compo 2001 (C64CGC).

198206.overview:
The Soultron star system has been at peace for millenniums, the echoes of warfare long faded, its people living in hope for a never-ending peaceful existence.

Yet some had looked out into the skies, wondering what lay beyond, and what dangers could descend upon their peaceful worlds. In secret they developed project Soul Force, an advanced space fighter designed to defend the Soultron system from an outside threat.

And from the darkness of deep space comes a terrible bio-mechanical fleet swarming into the Soultron star system, monstrous creations descending upon the peaceful planets, tearing into the ground for reasons unknown. Communication attempts remain unanswered, the invaders obliterating any ship brave enough to approach...

We have chosen you to launch and pilot the new Soul Force space fighter against this terrifying threat and liberate our star system. Learn our enemy’s plans and put a stop to them for good. The fate of our star system lies in our hands. You are our last and only hope...

198342.overview: Slotmeister is a computerized simulation of a video slot machine. It was developed by Willaim Laabs and published in Loadstar #137 in 1995.

198429.overview: Subtraction Tic Tac Toe is a math based Tic Tac Toe game that revolves around subtraction. It is a conversion of an old Commodore Plus/4 game. The conversion was done by Barry "Cout" Hart in 2017.

198450.overview: Scavenger: Neat and Clean is a simple space shooter coded entirely in BASIC. It was developed by GH-23 for the BASIC-Game Compo 2010.

198452.overview:
Chessboard Nim is a mathematical puzzle game played on a board resembling a chess or checker board. It was published as a type-in program in the 1983 book  "Games Commodore 64 Computers Play"

It was also released in The Netherlands under the name Schaakbord Nim in the Dutch version of the book, which was titled "Het Commodore 64 Computer-Spelen Boek" which came out a year later.

198800.overview: Snek is a simple, but fun snake clone for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Bernd Lietzow and released into the public domain in 2018

198801.overview:
Snertle is a math game for kids that involves a cute little turtle. It was developed by Soori Sivakumaran and published in COMPUTE! 1984/05 (Issue #48). "Snertle" is designed to help teacli cliildren the fundamentals of addition, subtraction, and multiplication. A turtle named Snertle is drawn on the screen to give encouragement and assistance to the player. 
 
Snertle allows children to tailor math problems to fit their individual abilities and weaknesses. Snertle first asks the child to select addition, sub- traction, or multiplication problems. If addition or subtraction is selected, the child is then asked to choose the largest and smallest numbers to be used in creating the problems. The largest number that can be chosen is 99 and the smallest number is zero. If multiplication is chosen, the child can de- cide to practice a certain "times table," or solve problems created randomly from through the 14 times table. For example, if the 12 times table is selected, then one number in each question created will always be 12. The other number will be randomly selected from the range 0-14.  
 
If the child chooses to attempt random multi- plication problems, he or she must define the range of numbers (within the limits of and 14) from which the problems can be created, similar to the process for random addition or subtraction problems.

199308.overview: In all different settings, go from one base to another in your helicopter, avoiding monsters and mountains. Published in Hebdogiciel Software N°1.

199310.overview: To defend your planet you must join your ship hidden underground in a labyrinth. Published in Hebdogiciel Software N°1.

199311.overview: 5 action mini-games written by Frédéric Miran and published in Hebdogiciel Software N°1.

199510.overview: To risk your life for a few goldfish, is it really reasonable? Left to drop bomb (clears obstacles), fire for temporary invisibility, and up/down to move your swimmer. Created by François Lavialle. Published in France in Hebdogiciel Hors Serie N°2, and in Hebdogiciel Software N°3.

199525.overview: By the precision of your shot, spare the earth from the evil presence of some harmful space borne creatures. A shooter created by Jean-Philippe Pasquier and published in Hebdogiciel Hors Serie N°2, and in Hebdogiciel Software N°6.

199545.overview: This is a 2021 updated version of an earlier game simply called Bart Simpson (also from the same developer) The goal is simple, you are Bart and you have to jump over various Simpsons characters on your skateboard.

199871.overview:
A scientist has been captured by a villainous tyrant who is now trying to force him to make gold for him. The main hero of the adventure, i.e. the player, actually stumbles into this story by accident. But as it should be for an adventurer and hero, this challenge is of course accepted.

Will it be possible to obtain the Philosopher's Stone, that mystical elixir that can turn everything into gold?

And if so, what will happen then?

200311.overview: Created by Corkey Wood and published both by Nibbles & Bits, Inc. and in 75 Spill Datatronic also known as Super Frog,  this Frogger style game, unlike many others, even those with very similar names, has three avoidance areas, first the regular interstate of cars, trucks and trailers, then a section where you must avoid the aliens and bugs before getting through the traditional logs, lily-pads and crocs.

200322.overview: Space Joust is a single player German language clone of the arcade classic, Joust. It was published by Roeske Verlag in Computerposter 1984/08.

200369.overview: This is a shuffleboard style game for 2 players. Each player has 4 counters, each player has different colored counters. The computer will ask the players the row they would like to place the counter in. Then you must press the F7 key and the longer you hold it the farther the counter will slide. You must vary the rows you are allowed to use. Published as a game of "The Big 100" collection.

200394.overview: Smasheroids is a 1-2 player (not simultaneous) clone of the arcade classic, Asteroids for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Scott Elder and published in Loadstar #72 in 1990.

200454.overview: Shiutterbug's Pictures is a single player memory game. It was developed by LITAG Productions and published in Loadstar #75 in 1990.

200456.overview: A memory party game where you try to repeat the pattern given as Simon says. Written by Dave Lundberg and initially released for the Commodore PET and packaged in a way that ran them in a form of emulation on the C64.

200506.overview: A further development on the concept of Survival Messenger V1.1, with many more rooms, degrees of freedom and much higher complexity. A text adventure created by the teams at The 7th Division and Vintage Computing Carinthia. You wake up with a cramp starting in your left toe and sand in your mouth.  What has happened you can not remember.  Wind brings a salty breeze and on an island nobody else is there.You are stranded on an unknown island and you find a mobile phone where strangers, who are more or less attentive, give you advice via instant chat.

200640.overview:
Spirit of Ben Hur (also known as Ben Hur Challenge and Ben Hur) is a solitaire card game developed by Knees Calhoon and G.F. Collins. It was published in Loadstar #169 in 1998.

Rules/gameplay:

There are two goals to the game: try to build UP the foundations by suit from the ace to the king; and
try to do it with as few spins of the tableau as Possible.

The aces are removed from the deck and placed in the "Colosseum area" forming the four foundations. Then fourteen cards are dealt around the foundations The rest of the cards are placed face down and turned one at a time to a Single waste Pile.

The top card of the waste pile is available for play to the tableau or the foundations. Cards in the tableau Can be played to the foundation only if they are in the same row or the same column as
the foundation Pile.

There is no building in the tableau. Empty spaces in the tableau may be filled from the waste Pile only.
The game is won if all cards are built to the foundation.

The game can be played with either a joystick or a mouse.

200732.overview:
A faithful C64 port of the arcade classic of the same name. This version was made in 2021 by Mariano Kalafatovich.

Game description: 

Earth is under attack from rows of bomb dropping aliens, and you need to defend it! The rows of aliens begin at the top of the screen, and you control a laser cannon at the bottom of the screen. Your goal is to earn points by shooting the aliens before they can land. The aliens march back and forth, and each time the end of the screen is reached they will drop one row closer to the bottom. Shoot them all, and you move on to the next (tougher) level, but if even one of them lands the game is over. From time to time a flying saucer will pass by along the top of the screen; shoot this to earn extra points. Just above your laser cannon are three shields; these can be used to hide from the alien's bombs, but will also block your own shots. You begin the game with a limited number of laser cannons, and if all of them are bombed the game ends.

200736.overview:
Developed by Karsten Senkel, you must battle waves of enemies and the more enemies you destroy the higher your score. Certain enemies give more points such as the emperor giving you 500 and the Torcher 750 points. The game features 12 different enemy types, asteroid fields, boss battles, power ups, ship and weapon upgrades, a balanced difficulty curve, and developed for PAL systems but will also run (a little faster) on NTSC.

Sold as part of the BOBR games Space Collection.


This is a clone/unofficial port of the 1980 arcade game Space Firebird.

200780.overview: A great looking Star Trek game created by SteveBoy aka István Maros. Star date 48308.2, it is your mission as a member of the Star Ship Voyager NCC-74656 to assist repairs to the ship by solving the logic, memory and puzzle games and repair the various systems. Failures can raise the alert status to Yellow Alert and then to Red Alert if things go very poorly. Keep your cool, use your mind and follow the prime directive when convenient.

201579.overview: Space Panic is a clone/unofficial conversion of the Universal arcade game of the same name for the Commodore 64. This version was developed by Karmic in 2021 and published into the public domain.

201810.overview: Space Fiend: The Terror Begins is a 1-2 player (co-op) vertically scrolling shmup developed by Dan "ACE" Dare using Chris Yates' SEUCK engine. The year of release is currently unknown.

202037.overview: Not to be confused with Snake Byte from Sirius Software, Snake Bite is a public domain Snake clone with some puzzle elements. This game was developed by Alan Bond in 1988.

202164.overview:
You'd think it was a "minesweeper" game by the title but its really a fast-paced and really tough shooter. Released as Strasdenian in Italy in International Games n.8 (settembre 1991).  
 
You are on patrol in the skies of Frekkel orbital station when aliens are spotted approaching. Thus begins your battle against the strange and menacing beings who want to conquer the world. You must fly (being careful not to hit the buildings) and destroy the aliens that appear on your dial with your laser cannon. You have to be very careful as they are very fast and often have unpredictable movements. At the end of the squadron of enemies you will have to face the Strasdenian support ship which is very powerful and must be hit many times to destroy. If you can get past the support ship make your way to a tougher level with a mothership at the end.

202408.overview: A second version of Shiver Me Tumbers also by Dana Clapp, this version with different presentation\graphics and an adjusted story line. You still need to escape the island and solve the mystery therein. Published in Loadstar #036.

202411.overview: Find out if you are like Simon Le Bon of Duran Duran by taking this Quiz in Italian. The male counterpart to a similarly formatted game about Madonna. Published in Edizione Logica 2000 Supplementi #04 - Speciale n.01 - Squinzie, Sfitinzie & Paninari 64.

202430.overview:
Are you like Madonna? Leafing through the biography of Madonna Luise Ciccone it is evident that she is quite eccentric. In fact, in the recounting of her past loves there are blonde and brown men, musicians like Dan Gilroy, disk-jockeys, drummers and actors like her current husband, Sean Penn. All varied from each other but united in by the fact that they are young, ambitious and full of artistic talent. If you want to know if you are similar to her you can take the quiz and see. It isn't that you won't answer correctly for yourself, you just might not be of the same type. 

Published in Italy in Edizione Logica 2000 Supplementi #04 - Speciale n.01 - Squinzie, Sfitinzie & Paninari 64.

202628.overview: It is a hard life for the friendly forest dwellers! The Smurfette is lost and a villager needs to go find her and bring her back safely home. The game consists of a long path full of pitfalls and obstacles that you must avoid and overcome only by dodging and jumping. You will meet many animals that you absolutely must not touch, or lose one of your three lives. You will have to move, even in the creepy darkness.

202690.overview:
The Sky Is Falling is the fantastic debut C64 release from Stuart Collier, based on an original game by Ovine by Design, assisted with graphics by Trevor Storey and funky soundtracks from Richard Bayliss.  The game will be packaged in authentic 'Imagine' style packaging, making it a great collector's item for C64 fans!


Story:
The intrepid explorer Orangeman is having a really bad day!  Not only is the roof of the cave he is exploring collapsing but he is being chased by a massive boulder as well!  Luckily he brought a bunch of tools with him which he can hurl at the cave roof to smash the sharp stalactites that are descending towards him.  Can you help Orangeman escape from the caves before he is squished?

202691.overview:
Sky Blast is a simple Blitz/Bomber clone. Like other games of this nature, your goal is to destroy all the buildings so you can safely land your plane.

This version was developed by Suman Roy and published in Your Computer 1986/03.

203087.overview:
Santa's Busy Day is a somewhat primitive Pac-Man style game for the Commodore 64. However in this game, instead of playing the typical Pac-Man character, you play as Santa Claus trying to save Christmas.

This game was developed by George Trepal and was originally published in the December 1985 issue of Ahoy! magazine. It was also published in 2004 in GO64! 2004/12.

203725.overview:
Section Pi is a side scrolling sci-fi shooter. The player moves the ship to the right and has the task of shooting down or avoiding enemy units, avoiding hitting the upper and lower limits of the tunnel. At the end of each stage there is a final boss.

It was developed by Mariusz Jakubowski and published in the October 1990 version of COMPUTE!'S Gazette, which at the time was no longer published separately, but published as an insert in COMPUTE! magazine.

204204.overview:
It is the year 2197. An alien planet, Zarjon has spiraled out of control and is heading towards planet Earth. We have sent in a few pilots and scientists to find out what has caused this planet to fly so quickly towards our planet. It turns out that a crystal stored in the bottom of the mines appears to be the source. Our people tried to remove the crystal in order to stop the planet but they got destroyed by the alien forces.

This is where you come in. Your mission is to enter the alien planet Zarjon. Fly through the 4 underground lairs and do battle against the aliens. You must ten located the crystal and destroy it in order to save Earth.

Your ship is charged with a limited number of shields. These will be lost if you collide into any aliens, their lasers or any other obstacles you come across. Once all of your shields are out our hope will be lost and Earth will be destroyed. You will be awarded an extra shield for every level completed also 1,000 points will be awarded as a bonus for you.

Can you find the power crystal and destroy it or will life on Earth be no more? The fate of Earth lies in your hands.

Good luck Pilot.

204718.overview:
Adventure is a series of fourteen text adventure and graphic adventure games primarily written by Scott Adams and published by Adventure International. The twelve originals were re-released with graphics as Scott Adams Graphic Adventures (SAGA).

First remake of the series,  SAGA#1: Adventureland had many additional features including  graphics, Text-to-Speech hardware support &upper- and lowercase support for display.

Gameplay was very similar to the original. You still used the same one or two word commands to move about and manipulate objects. The RETURN key toggled back and forth between graphics and text.

The objective of the game is to collect all the treasures. There are all sorts of places to explore above and below ground. You have to outwit and escape many creatures during your quest including a dragon, a bear, and a hive of bees.

204787.overview: The Soul Gem of Martek was yet another mysterious title which went astray since some initial mentions in magazines and adverts.  This was a title that was to be released back in 1985 by Anirog, and was to be a text adventure – mixed with arcade elements.

205051.overview: The player competes in a series of one-on-one matches against a series of computer-controlled opponents or in a single match against another player. Each match consists of three rounds in which the player must defeat an opponent in less than 30 seconds. If a match ends before a fighter is knocked out, then the fighter with the greater amount of energy left will be declared the round's winner. The player must win two rounds in order to defeat the opponent and proceed to the next battle. If the third round ends in a tie, then the computer-controlled opponent will win by default or both players will lose. During the single-player mode, the player can continue after losing and fight against the opponent they lost the match to. Likewise, a second player can interrupt a single-player match and challenge the first player to a new match.

205060.overview: Shaana: Asteroid is an Italian language graphic text adventure with a science fiction theme. It was developed Alessandro Zanello and published by Edizioni Società SIPE srl. in Adventure 64 N.2 in 1986.

205373.overview:
Shove is a cross between an "avoid-it" game and a puzzle game. Manoeuvre your green ball/blob around the maze while avoiding obstacles (including balls/blobs of other colors) until you reach the exit. Touching the walls can also result in a loss of life.

Shove was developed and released by The Vinyl Projects in 1998. It was their only game.

205430.overview:
Samu 2 is a 1-2 player (co-op) vertically scrolling shooter developed and released by Outlaw-Emix Software in 1991. 

Shoot the animals that have gone amok.

205446.overview: The evil Star Hawx threaten to take over the Galaxy. Earth has had enough and has decided to fight back. You control a space fighter, which has to do battle against all of the Star Hawx. Use left/right to move your ship and fire to blast lasers at those deadly birds.The Space Hawx will attempt to avenge and attack against your fighter. As soon as all of the Star Hawx have been shot dead, you will be awarded a bonus of 1000 points and move onto the next level, where the game gets harder. At any time during play, use down to protect yourself via a shield. Once the shield is gone, it is gone. Shoot green eggs to be awarded a shield and a mystery bonus. Can you complete all 16 levels battling against the evil Star Hawx? Good luck pilot.

205669.overview:
Andrea writes: First of all, thank you for your wonderful vault. I always loved the whole SEUCK scene... and now here I am, two decades later, looking for some enlightenment about SEUCK. Exactly 20 years ago I made a game with SEUCK called "Slaughterland". I think it's a quite interesting game, since it tries to tweak the SEUCK possibilities in order to create bonuses, enormous end-of-level bosses, hidden routes and so on. Nothing you haven't seen before, but, still, it's a original SEUCK game not yet shared online or offline. Problem is, that back in 1989 I only had a tape cassette recorder. I managed to transfer from tape to PC only the "finished game" as a .TAP image, while the other files (ie the "ALL DATA" one) are lost. I'd really like to share the game, but I'd also like to re-edit it here and there to make it more enjoyable... I tried the "SEUCK REVIVE" tool by Entropia but it didn't work for me (maybe because of the .TAP format?)

What I'm asking is: do you, SEUCK gurus, know any other way of restoring my game from the "finished game" grave? It would be great if you could extract the data: I'd love to rearrange things a bit - as you'll notice, the difficulty level makes the game nearly impossible to complete (without cheats/savestates). Moreover, I was 14 when I created the game, so the texts are very silly and written in bad English. I'm still proud of the level played inside a jelly monster's belly, thou. With the final fight in the mouth of the monster itself, battling against his... teeth.

The data was not altered in any way, since I wasn't (and I'm not) able to fiddle with code, assembly and stuff like that (and it's a pity, since the "SEUCK REDUX" tool seems sooo interesting).

205672.overview: A Shoot'em Up created with the SEUCK and released in 1988 based on important Italian politicians of the 80's such as Eugenio Scalfari. A 2005 update was released by the original creators, AEG Soft.

205718.overview:
Space Gallery is a fast paced fixed screen space shooter for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Jeff A. Lapkoff and published in the following:

-   COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1985/07 (Issue #25)
-   Best of COMPUTE! & Gazette, 
-   64'er Spielesammlung #6

Blast those hostile aliens to their doom before they blast you to yours. Disgusting sky dogs occupied space. You should create dog-free zones. In infinity, that's damn hard!

205720.overview:
Sleuth is a text-based murder mystery strategy game that borrows influences from board games like Clue, but also stuff such as Sherlock Holmes. It was developed by Kevin Mykytyn and published in the following:

-   COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1985/07 (Issue #25)
-   Best of COMPUTE! & Gazette
-   COMPUTE!'s Third Book of C64 Games

205721.overview:
Slavic Law is yet another solitaire game developed by the most prolific developer of C64 solitaire games, Maurice Jones. This one was developed in the year 2000, and release in Loadstar #198.

The Game:

One king is removed from a double deck of cards and placed to the left. Turn cards from the deck to the queen, spreading them downward. When another king is turned, the computer will place it to the right of the first pile and the process is continued until all the cards have been turned. The top card of each pile is available for play at all times.

As they become available, the aces are played in a row above the kings to form the foundation. The aces are built upward without regard to suit to the jack. The queens are dead cards and are moved, as they are turned, to a pile to the left of the layout. The player may arrange the foundations in any way he/she chooses.

The object is to build all cards except the kings and queens to the foundations.

If all covering cards are removed from a king, any available card may be played there, but only after all cards have been turned from the deck.

The game can be played with either a joystick, keyboard, and even a properly configured mouse.

205937.overview: Shogun is a simple adventure game. It was developed by Robert Wallace and published by ComputerMat in it's "Samurai Pak" in 1983.

205941.overview:
Shogun is based on the Japanese board game Hasami Shogi. A piece can only move forward, sideways, or backward. Diagonal moves are not allowed. A piece can move to an adjacent empty square, or junp any adjacent piece (the attacker's or the defender's) and land on an empty square. The jumped piece is NOT captured. White always moves first.

A piece is captured by squeezing it between two of the attacker's pieces. That is, when the attacker gets one on either side (except diagonal) of a defender's piece, the defender's piece is captured. Captured pieces are removed from play. A piece is not captured if it moves between two pieces. There are no double moves.

In the original game, to win, you had to capture all of your opponent's pieces. This version has optional victory conditions. The game came be won by the first player to capture a specified number of pieces in a specified number of turns.

This game was developed by Lance C. Thomas and published in Loadstar #187.

206587.overview: An unofficial Star Trek text adventure for the Commodore 64. The game was developed by Detlef Ackermann and released into the public domain. The year of release is not currently known.

206596.overview: Star Video Poker (also known as Loadstar's Video Poker) is a casino video poker game developed by John Serafino in 1996. It was published in Loadstar #142. Plays with Joystick (in port 1) or a Commodore mouse.

206597.overview: Stormbird is a public domain black and white vertically scrolling shooter for the Commodore 64. The game is similar to games like 1942, but with also a bit of River Raid thrown in for good measure. It was developed by Anthony Burns for the 2010 Vertically Scrolling SEUCK Competition. It was also released as part of Commodore Free #067.

206656.overview:
Despite its name, Slots is not a slot machine simulation, rather it is a variation of the childhood favorite, four in a row (better known by the trademarked name of Connect Four) created by Roger Silva and published originally in COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1986/08 (Issue #38), and then later in SYS PD Diskett#20 (1991). Match wits with a very intelligent opponent — your computer. An intriguing four-level strategy game. 

Can you outsmart your computer? "Slots" is a strategy game which challenges you to out-think your machine. You and the computer take turns dropping tokens into a box with eight vertical slots. To win, you must get four of your tokens in a row vertically, horizontally, or diagonally. Or you can win by being first to put a token at the top position of any slot in the box. Each time you select one of the eight rows in which to place a token, it's dropped to the lowest available position in that slot. Each slot is then filled from bottom to top during play. The game is tricky, though: What often seems to be a good move might be just the stepping stone the computer needs to win.

206667.overview:
Initially published in COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1984/08 (Issue #14) / a.k.a. "Snowcar", it was later released in Ahoy! 1986/05 (Issue #29) as Ski Folly and then in Robtek's Slalom. The Sno-Cat is a super-powered turbo-driven tractor that can go zero to fifty in less than a second. It has a minor problem, however: It shifts its own gears. It starts in second, shifts into third automatically after ten seconds, then into fourth 
after fifty seconds. It can't go any higher, but it doesn't need to. It's difficult to maintain control in third gear, let alone fourth. 

Fortunately you have brakes, very powerful brakes that will slow you down to almost zero in tricky situations. To stop overuse, the brakes (controlled by the fire button or space bar) cause the distance meter to stop as long as the brakes are pressed. But the timer still runs, so your time may be impaired by using the brakes too much.

206668.overview: A racing collect-em-up game created for the Commodore PET by Malcolm Michael and adapted for the Commodore 64 by Steven Darnold of New Zealand. It was released in the Red Pack games compilation and published in Australia and New Zealand by Street Games.

206673.overview: Scorpion is a solitaire variant. If was developed by Maurice Jones and published in Loadstar #179 in 1999. A "Choose your interface" solitaire game that would be a royal hassle if you had to deal out real cards. Scorpion is one of those games in which piles can grow almost without limit. If you were to have to actually handle these cards it would be an onerous task. Although all suits are to be built in the tableau, this is at its essence a 'build to the foundation' type game. Most games have a 10% win rate and there is considerable chance for strategy.

206677.overview:
Scorpion is a 1988 horizontal scrolling shooter developed by Leslie Wigmore and published in the following:

-   Commodore Disk User 1988/09-10
-   Your Commodore 1990/11 (Tape #10) 
 
Big place, the Galaxy. But not big enough. It's all summed up in Semionovich's First Law, a sociological corollary of the famous Lorentz-Fitzgerald equations. Semionovitch broadly stated that, just as it is completely unfeasible to achieve the speed of light within the constraints of normal space- time, it is similarly impossible for any intelligent life form to attain the point at which it is satisfied with its supply of resources and living space. Of course, just as the Lorentz-Fitzgerald equations were overthrown by Grace's Hypergeometry Theory in 2243, so Semionovitch may yet be disproved. Tell it to the Space Marines. Our job, as an unbiased multi-racial peacekeeping force is to keep those lifeforms who insist on obeying the Semionovitch dictums in line (the expression 'blowing them away' is frowned on in the modem SM. We prefer keeping the peace with maximum prejudice'). The finest tool of the Space Marines is the galaxy fighter Scorpion. 

Now you too can sample the danger and excitement that a spell in the Space Marines offers you. Just drop in at your local recruiting office and ask to try our Scorpion simulator. You will incur no obligation. We stress that the brain-to-computer input techniques used in the Scorpion simulator are entirely non-invasive -only the sensory centres of the brain are stimulated. The fact that 99 percent of simulation users subsequently join up can simply be attributed to the excellent terms and conditions of service contained in our standard 99-year contract. Well what are you waiting for, kid? Hit that simulation. We'll see you in the Marines.

206678.overview: Scorpion II is the sequel to Leslie Wigmore's sidescrolling space shooter, Scorpion. This sequel was published in Your Commodore 1991/07 (Tape #19).

206679.overview: A Worm\Snake game published in COMPUTE! 1984/04 (Issue #47) and in the Street Games "Red Box" release in Australia and New Zealand. The game is featuring Nerm the Worm, who is trapped in Bemer Castle and would like nothing more than to escape (and consume a generous helping of "magic mushrooms" along the way). Yet another variation on Snake where the player controls a serpentine crawler in perpetual motion, which must be guided to consume food, dodge deadly walls, and avoid biting its own tail. The castle is composed of eleven rooms, each trickier to navigate than the last. In a vaguely Carrollian manner, the rooms are prone to sprouting mushrooms which cause Nerm to grow as he eats them: after consuming five mushrooms, the exit doors will open, leading to the next room. Extra lives are awarded along the way, presumably another effect of the magical fungi.

206936.overview:
Santa's Boulder Dash Party is a game developed by Arno Weber using Peter Liepa's Boulder Dash Construction Kit. It has a Christmas theme and the main character is edited to resemble Santa Claus.

It was released to the public domain in 2004.

207147.overview:
This is a remake/conversion of the Activision Atari 2600 game Seaquest for Commodore 64. 

The aim is to rescue stranded divers, avoid sharks and enemy submarines, and not run out of oxygen. You can refill your oxygen by going to the surface at the cost of one diver. If you surface with no rescued divers, you lose a life. However if you surface with six divers, you get a nice bonus based on how much oxygen you have left. This is called a "round".

After each round the enemies become faster, their number increases, and destroying them gives you more points. After two rounds an enemy sub starts patrolling the surface too. You gain an extra life every 10000 points, maximum six in reserve.

Use joystick in port 2 to play. If you are using an emulator, make sure the borders are enabled and visible.

Except for a couple of minor details, the original Atari 2600 manual applies to this port.

207257.overview: Snot and Crap is a 1-2 player (co-op) game developed by Cyber Systems using the Shoot 'em Up Construction Kit. While you do have to climb ladders, it is not considered a platformer due to the nature of SEUCK games, it's basically a vertically scrolling shooter in which you have to move in front of the ladders in order to advance up the screen.

207260.overview:
Solar Quest is a 2001 science fiction themed pinball game for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Tim Vik and published in Loadstar #206.

Control the flippers by moving the joystick left and right.

207320.overview:
From the developer of the C64 port of Prince of Persia and Donkey Kong Jr. comes Sonic the Hedgehog, a faithful port of the Sega Master System version of the game.

This port requires REU emulation (in VICE, click on the settings tab, then click on settings, then cartridges, then RAM Expansion Module, and make sure you choose a minimum of 512K, but it doesn't hurt to choose higher).

This port was released on December 19, 2021.

Description:

To stop the evil Dr. Robotnik, Sonic must traverse six zones consisting of three levels each. Most of the zones are based on those in the original game, but some are entirely new, including a jungle environment and a huge airship. Other unique differences are one level that scrolls automatically and one that is aligned vertically instead of horizontally. Most of the enemies (mechanized animals, defeated by Sonic's spikes when jumping or rolling) and power-ups (speed-ups, shields, extra lives) are the same as in the Genesis version as well. Sonic can pick up golden rings for protection (when hit, he simply loses all of his rings instead of a life) and bonuses: 100 rings gain Sonic an extra life, and 50 remaining rings at the end of a level allow access to pinball-themed special stages full of bumpers and springs. The final level of a zone is always a boss fight against Robotnik. Some of the boss fights differ in the Master System and Game Gear versions of the game, with special designs for the handheld version due to the smaller visible screen area.

Sonic should also collect the six Chaos Emeralds to keep them from falling into Robotnik's hands. In a departure from the original game, these are not hidden in the special stages but somewhere in the regular levels.

Code and SFX: Andreas "Mr. Sid" Varga
Graphics: Oliver "Veto" Lindau
Music:  Mikkel "Encore" Hastrup

207369.overview: One of the many games simply called "Space" for C64, this one is an arcade shooter published in German programming magazine "Computer Programmiert zur Unterhaltung", or "Computer Programs for Entertainment"

207447.overview: Game description: Scramble your fighter and take on the enemy base in this modern take of the arcade classic. Guide your ship through varied and mountainous terrain to infiltrate an enemy base and destroy it! Scramble Infinity is a modern day remake of the original Scramble arcade game featuring improved graphics and sonics while retaining the same game play elements.

207491.overview:
Santa's Workout is a brand new Commodore 64 puzzle game.

Build your way to the exit across 24 exciting puzzles.

The game has a password system to load already played levels.

Santa's Workout is tested on TheC64 and VICE emulator.

The game will run in PAL and NTSC modes, but it's not optimized for NTSC.

207542.overview: Ski: The Seven Devils Ski Race is a simple downhill skiing game for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Gary V, Fields and released as part of the ReRUN Gamepack Disk in 1985. A downhill race with obstacles such as trees, gates and even the Devil!

207552.overview: Sam's Journey Season Special is a special holiday themsed challenge level of Sam's Journey developed as a free mini-game aimed at expert players of Sam's Journey. It was released on Christmas Eve of 2021.

208233.overview:
Steeplechase is a 2 player only split screen horse riding/racing game for the Commodore 64.  Jump over walls, trees, fences, an other objects, and the first person to reach the course length (selectable between 1,2,3) wins the race, and then it goes back to the title screen.

The game was developed by Tony Brantner and published in Ahoy! 1987/08 (Issue #44)

208310.overview:
It's Christmas Eve!

Your longest night is nearing its end when you discover that, in a small town, rats have joined forces with other animals to fill houses with dangerous presents as revenge for the traps\n
So your task doubles: not only will you have to deliver the right presents under the Christmas trees, but you'll have to remove the bad ones - all before morning comes.



A little new-old Xmas C64 game, by Marco Giorgini (with an original soundtrack by Andrea Capitani)

A special thanks to Eric Akeson for his priceless testing time.



This is my first C64 game. I really hope you enjoy it. If so, and if you have the time, I'll be really happy if you help spread it around by sharing your gameplay or talking about it.



Ah, this game is free. I won't mind a few dollars for a coffee or a beer, but they're not really necessary. If you have something extra to share, please do so with those close to you who may be having a better day for a little unexpected surprise.

Hey, it is Christmas after all :-)



Some general notes about the game: 

- the complete game is the full version. It's the one with 9 different levels and a game movement change while going on playing again them with less time - if you're able to beat them.  The game has not a specific end - it's you against your top score (that won't be saved once you leave, sorry).
The original version (released before Xmas) has just the first three levels (and then goes on repeating with them).

- exploding gifts give you more points, so if you can it's better to take them in order (after a trembling one check where's the new next one)

- rats and bats defeat you with a single touch, so watch out when you jump even for animals moving on the above level

- inside walls with a hole in the lower part leave rats running thru them, while of course you can't (this will happen in levels 4-5-6-7-8-9)

- holes in the background (black) walls let the rats to move from a room to another one, even on a different floor (this will happen in levels 7-8-9)

208451.overview:
The Stalingrad Campaign is a 1 - 2 player war game based upon the Nazi invasion of the USSR during World War II.

Designed for 1 - 2 players, each player controls the major land forces of either Nazi or Soviet forces. A computer opponent is available for 1-player games. The viewpoint is of the general staff, and every turn the player is given objectives from either Moscow or Berlin to take control of a specific location on the map, while also being given forbidden locations. The player is ultimately judged by how well they meet the demands of headquarters, and how each country fares against historical standards. The game is text-only, and came with a board and physical pieces to allow the player to keep track of the location of theirs and enemy units.

Each turn encompasses 1 week, and there are four separate scenario choices. During each turn, the player can review reports from the front lines, as well as reports from individual units and headquarters. During this phase, the player can also issue orders for their troops, including setting movement objectives and posture for their units. They can also assign supply priorities, location of air corps, and can move their different headquarters to enable better communication.

After setting orders, the computer distributes supplies and automatically calculates movement and combat results of the individual units, and the player receives results of battle action. Fog of war is a constant through battle, and the player can lose track of their own or enemy units if their communication is cut off, and the player never receives entirely accurate reports of enemy location and movements.

208763.overview:
In this classic game you play as ' Roderrick Hero ' and must search the cave system for the miners of Mount Leone, who have been trapped deep below after a recent volcanic situation that has occurred. The game features multiple levels, different themed underground areas, dangerous enemies such as spiders, and dynamite to blow up walls to reach the miners trapped below.

A C64 game created using only sprites for the Only Sprites Compo

208766.overview: Created originally for Christmas 1993, this arcade collect-em up game has you helping Saint Nick to make his appointed rounds.Unfortunately, the old guy had a bit too much eggnog and dumped presents all over the country. The aim with this game is to collect 99 presents before the time runs out. It was later re-released in GO64! 2004/12.

208768.overview:
A fine new shmup collection for your commie at itchi ! the Sarah Jane Avory contains 3 Shoot em ups for your c64 pleasures. So copy it on your floppy from itch.io.

Contains:
Neutron v1.3 +7HD
Santron +7HD 
Zeta Wing v1.1 +6D

208770.overview:
Originally created for the ZX Spectrum in 1994, this game was officially ported to multiple platforms as part of Zenobi Software's New "25th Anniversary" DAAD Version.  
 
In the stereotypical magical kingdom of Kwargz, the peace and quiet had been shattered by the arrival of the evil orc-lord Beydm - a being with far too many consonants in his name!

The orc-lord and his troops had taken to holding all-night parties, which were greatly disapproved of by the local natives - mainly because they were never invited. Eventually, after the orc's annual spate of "hobbit bashing", things got too much for the poor people to bear and YOU were called upon to help.

YOU are not a "bold warrior" or an "elf" or even a "mighty wizard". YOU are a sadly pathetic little person who will use any excuse at all to take part in an adventure full of "thrills" and "high excitement" - or at least its nearest equivalent for £2.49 or less.

And so YOU find yourself on a quest to obtain the only item that can rid the land of these orcs - Jeremy's Fabled Golden Camcorder - the most orc-terrifying object in the entire universe. In fact legend has it that it can even create more fear and loathing than an invitation to have tea with a Balrog.

Legend also has it that the infamous camcorder can only be found in one place ... the even more infamous and highly mysterious area known as "THE NETHER REGIONS". None have ever returned from there - if only for the simple reason that nobody knows how to get there in the first damn place! - so your task will be a fairly simple one.

Just find out where the "Nether Regions" are, make your way there and recover the Golden Camcorder ... easy!!!!!

208778.overview: A simple, but funny and oddly enjoyable action game created by Raffaele Formato, Raffox, and Michael Zuurman. Control your sheep and jump the obstacles. For every screen of success things will become a bit more complex.

208786.overview: A dueling shooter created for the Commodore 64 Crap Game Compo 2006 (C64CGC). Navigate your pachyderm around the arena and fireball your frenemy before they get you.

208796.overview:
One Player Fun Arcade Like Shoot 'em' up, Shoot the Aliens, Pick up Bonus ball, Get to the End and do it all over again.

Made with the Shoot 'Em' Up Construction Kit by Sensible Software and with added Seuck Enhancment Framework v3 by Richard Bayliss of TND.

208798.overview: The SID Chip Club is my new C64\Cartridge album featuring techno and house tracks, played back by a 1980s Commodore 64 home computer. The limitations of that machine and its legendary 3-voice sound chip called "SID", combined with some nifty programming, result in a special kind of sound.

208823.overview: This is a game that allows you to learn as much or as little about rockets and shuttles as you would like. But it is more than a role, you will be the rocket or shuttle designer. You will make the decisions and a vehicle will fly. How well it flies will depend on your decisions.

208826.overview:
A spelling game for the 64. Spell Maze is an educational game that's designed to help a student with spelling. Among other features, the game has several levels of words to spell arranged in varying degrees of difficulty.  
 
Published in COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1994/04, now again part of the main, renamed Compute magazine.

208854.overview: Your name is Henry Wilcox, an agent for MI-5, the British secret service. You are on vacation in West Berlin when you receive a call from John Dinkleberry, the commissioner of MI-5. He says, "Sorry to interrupt your vacation, Wilcox. But I have a top priority case for you."

208855.overview: A Galaga\Galaxian style shooter created by Frank Neuhaus. Swooper is a space shooter. The player has to transport a vaccine from Earth to a space station in which an epidemic has broken out. Unfortunately some aliens have something against this. The game is divided into two parts: during the first, the player is restricted to the bottom of the screen and has to shoot all alien ships which appear at the upper part. Alien shots are dodged by moving left or right. During the second part, the player has to survive a meteorite field. The player can change the speed of the ship - the faster, the more points are earned. While dodging, there are also astronauts to pick up which reward bonus points.

209087.overview: Super-Breakout is a simple Breakout clone from Germany for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Dillingersoft (Klaus Dillinger) and published in Compute mit 1985/10.

209203.overview: Slagalica (also known as Sestavljanka) is a Croatian language educational puzzle game for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Davor Bonacic, Darja Hudin, Matjaz Colnaric & Mitja Solar and published by Suzy Soft in 1988. Both titles (Slagalica and Sestavljanka translate to Puzzle)

209246.overview: Super-Penetrator is a side-scrolling shooter. Using missiles and bombs, the player must destroy air and ground objects on the way to the main base of the enemy. The fuel may be supplemented by hitting the ground containers. Released bombs falling on the gravity parabola, the missiles in exchange are moving along a straight line. Controlled fighter may be moved in any direction.

209248.overview:
An arcade style puzzle game created by Sören Kress & Jim Nowak, with music by Markus Schneider, it was published by Markt & Technik in both 64'er Sonderheft 66, and in Game On 1993/02. Two explorers land in unknown dimensions of time. Help them both find the time barrier so they can get return the present.  
 
In the year 2668, a much more convenient way of traveling to distant galaxies has long since been used: A special space capsule is bombarded with energy beams from the beam disintegrator at the A.T.I (Astral Travel Institute) until the probe is back in the desired solar system shows up. In this way, distances of light years can be overcome in a matter of seconds. However, this procedure has an undesired side effect: you end up in a non-predeterminable time dimension and have to try to reach the next time hole. The necessary time correction can then be made at any time with suitable instruments. The way to the time hole is paved with blocks of energy that you have to navigate with the probe on the correct course - otherwise you end up in nothing! Accompany the chrononauts on their way to safety!

209342.overview:
Experience all the thrills and Excitement of a day at the races in this icon driven simulation for up to 5 players.  
 
Not to be confused by the game of the same name by Virgin.

209621.overview: A birthday present for SIDWAVE in the form of a SEUCK shooter, created by Ras Bolding using Chris Yayes' famous construction kit.

209645.overview:
Silk Dust is a text adventure game running on many vintage platforms. It is the third chapter of a series of games, after Two Days to the Race and The Queen's Footsteps.  
 
Today is April 19, 1907. You, Emilia Vittorini, arrived yesterday in Varenna, on the shore of the beautiful Lake Como. You are hosted at the magnificent Villa Briccorosso; Princess Lucilla Briccorosso is preparing for the Silk Road Race, a 10,000km rally raid between Cairo in Egypt and Peking in China, to be done by car.

You represent ITA, founded by your father, the company that built the car the Princess just bought to use during the rally. The car is supposed to be delivered today. Your role will be to assist the delivery and make sure everything is perfectly functional.

210029.overview:
A game once released on the cover of Zzap 64 back in the day (Zzap!64 Megatape #30), a cool Galaxian type game by the creators of Orcus and possibly using some of its sprites. Haydn Dolly Dalton, Mike Ager, Jens-Christian Huus & Morten Sigaard Kristensen worked on another project together that was never independently released BUT was on the cover of Zzap64. The game was called "Subsonic".

It was a 2player simultaneous Galaxian type game. It was 100% complete and Mike may still have the original. I’m sure I still have the magazine and possibly the cassette with it on." This game was touted around various budget companies to make a quick buck for the developers, but sadly no-one took on the game. The developers then decided to sell the game to Zzap 64 for a quick profit, and the game was eventually released to the world through their cover mount. 

Good thing is that you can still play the game thanks to Zzap, and check out a rather nice game and a glimpse of some Orcus like techniques in a complete game by the developers.

210030.overview: A horizontally scrolling shooter for one player created by Mike Wacker and released for Mesec Corp. in 1983. This game would later be heavily modified and re-released as Annihilator, but the games are considered distinct.

210250.overview: Sea to Sea: The Transcontinental Railroad Game (also simply called Sea to Sea) is a 1993 railroad/train simulation for the Commodore 64. It was developed by David M. Moorman and was originally published in Loadstar #107. It was published again later in Loadstar #206.

210295.overview:
Sprite Invaders is a Space Invaders port made by C64 Demo Group Booze Designs for the Commodore 64.
Sprite Invaders features a new menu tune and displays only sprites with no chars or bitmaps!
This release is part of the Only Sprites Compo.

210330.overview: SID Hero is a Guitar Hero clone for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Zbigniew Ross (Zbych) and released into the public domain in 2016.

210345.overview:
A wonderful and surprising finding to enter the GTW64 archives, thanks to the efforts of Genesis Project in late February 2021.

Splish Splash is a previously unknown game that was intended for release on the Mastertronic budget label back in 1985. The game itself was written by Adrian Sheppard, who around the same time had/was converting One Man and His Droid to the C64. Adrian would later go on to develop Vampire and Grand Prix Simulator for Codemasters, as well as Pipe Mania for Empire.

The game was randomly found on an obscure set of Italian C64 disks as a frozen file, and has now been tidied up and bug fixed for release. Just how it got out is a mystery, though we suspect that the game was submitted to Mastertronic and someone there leaked the game out. We have managed to track down Adrian and hope to learn more shortly about the game and what happened to it exactly.

You must guide Splish through the factory using the lift to take him to each floor and place buckets under the holes in the pipes. When a bucket is full, or partly full, you must throw the water through a window at the left of each floor. A very simple, but fun concept overall which would have made a reasonably decent budget release at the time (especially compared to the guff like Bionic Granny that was released!).

So whilst we try and find out more about the background to game, waste no time in checking out the title for yourself and what has been a nice early surprise to 2021 thanks to the Genesis Project group!

210364.overview:
The story: You are Sparlok, the warrior wizard. Mage of the 33rd degree to the counsil of the Morning Star, Royal astronomer to King Hegel Pemborg I and keeper of the magical staff of Pleaedes. Now the kingdom of Toëffelbard has been overrun by the forces of the dark light. It is your task to restore order to the realm and to vanquish the Nine of Wormwood. Along the way you will have to battle undead skeletons, black scorpions, witches and other nasties. There is also a dragon that bars your way to victory. You will also pass by the magic tree of the 'knowledge of that which you don't know you know' (Isilmivtenib) and the river of blood. Slog your way through the Castle complex and eventually good shall triumph... well maybe.

The game was made using the Shoot 'em Up Construction Kit.

210385.overview: An update to the venerated Sublogic Flight Simulator II that was released in 1984 in combination with the more recent Master's XXL version. This release has enhanced and expanded scenery selections. It fixes the frequency display issues normally seen in the original game and makes the game much more enjoyable and playable.

210458.overview:
You are the soldier, Yeteran who has a tough mission on his hands. A space ship approached planet Earth and spawned out hoards of cheekily little aliens. They want to get rid of the human race, and take Earth as their own new home. You arm yourself with a pulse laser rifle and start zapping away at the aliens. Warning, your mission won't be all that easy. Since it is just one person against a large army of aliens. Good luck Yeteran.

Developed in 2016 by Roberto Ricioppo (who also did the music) using Chris Yates' Shoot 'em Up Construction Kit.

210515.overview: A horizontally scrolling shooter created by Adriano Pareto and published in the Jackson Soft Compilation #8 / no definite name, called "Missione" in the magazine.

210548.overview:
Suicide Solution, despite its dark sounding name, is actually just a simple 1-player Snake clone for the Commodore 64. The game was developed by Caesar and Mirage, with music by Geir Tjelta in 1991.

While the game was uncovered a few years back, it was never officially released.

210588.overview: Spectral Sneer is a Dueling game for one or two players released as a preview in 1987. You can control either a Wizard or a Warrior in a sideways scrolling platformer, where you can go underground or above ground, fighting with various enemies.

211007.overview:
Sever The Wicked! is a small fast-paced "coffee-break" shoot 'em up game. Destroy as many enemies as you can in 24 seconds! 

The further the enemy, the more points earned. Bosses grant extra points. Bonus points are given at the end of each round based on the number of enemies killed.

Try to get an unbroken combo going, combos are the key to getting higher scores.

211649.overview:
The Empire Strikes Back is an unofficial conversion of the Atari 2600/Mattel Intellivision game of the same name. This game was developed by a droup of people with the scene group Megastyle. Development of the game was started back in early 2020 with a couple of preview/playable demo versions released during the development time, but the full game was not released until May 4, 2022.

Game description:

Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back recreates a scene from the movie of the same name. You are on the icy planet of Hoth, and Imperial Walkers are closing in on the rebel power generator. As the pilot of a snowspeeder, you need to take out as many of the walkers as you can. The walkers are heavily armored, and it will take a lot of firepower to destroy one! The game is played on a large, scrolling screen with a radar screen at the bottom to help keep track of where the enemy is located. If a walker reaches the power generator, or you run out of snowspeeders the game is over. Good luck, and may the force be with you!

213280.overview: A Ghosts ‘n Goblins game for the Commodore 64 made in PETSCII, released 2022. If you loved playing the classic game of Ghosts 'n Goblins or Ghouls 'N Ghosts, then this latest version of the game for the C64 is pretty damn cool as not only is it a great nod to the classics, but think of it as a demake while made in PETSCII.

213289.overview: A work in progress (Read as Preview) single player platform game from Rhys B. Clatworthy. A find the keys style game but with an amazing, flame-shooting dragon character as the main character. There are baddies to defeat and bypass and energy "stars" to gather to find the keys to open the door to the next level.

213353.overview:
Compilation of games previously released individually in Europe by U.S. Gold

Featuring:

-    Gauntlet (conversion of the arcade classic)
-    Ace of Aces (flight combat simulator, originally published in North America by Accolade
-    Leaderboard (Golf game originally released in North America by Access Software)
-    Winter Games (Sports game originally released in North America by Epyx)
-    Infiltrator (a combination of a flight simulator and ground missions that involve stealth, originally released in North America by Mindscape)

213354.overview:
Space Waste is a public domain keyboard controlled fixed screen shooter for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Alan Bond and released in 1985.
Destroy the pink diamond shaped alien ships before they destroy you. This game was followed by a sequel: Adept - Space Waste II.

213423.overview:
Superstar Seymour is a five game compilation pack featuring the Seymour character.

These five games are:

-    Sergeant Seymour: Robot Cop
-    Seymour Goes to Hollywood
-    Stuntman Seymour
-    Super Seymour Saves the Planet
-    Wild West Seymour.

213426.overview: Space Hop is a Q*Bert inspired 3D platform game for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Duncan Scott Kershaw and released into the public domain in 1985.

213734.overview:
Shadowrun is a role-playing game for the Commodore 64 developed by Finnish coder Harri Holopainen and published in Floppy Magazine 1987/5.

Even though it was published in a Finnish disk magazine, the game is entirely in English.

214846.overview: Slangen is a Danish language Snake game for the Commodore 64. it was developed by Asger Alstrup and published in COMputer 1987 Vol.03 No.02 (January-February).

215495.overview:
CBM Poker Tournament (also called Speech Poker Tournament) is a single player poker game for the Commodore 64. It uses The Software Automatic Mouth (SAM) for the in-game speech. Despite being released and published by Commodore themselves, the game is considered slightly politically incorrect, as many of the opponents in the game utter words such as "arse, f*ck, and shit" when they have to fold.

The amount of money you start off is not a set amount. It starts with giving you a random amount of money.

215566.overview: Suspense is a solitaire card game variant for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Maurice Jones and published iin Loadstar #198. In this version of Suspense all the cards are dealt face up to give a greater chance for use of strategy. The layout is supposed to be four, six-card pyramids. Each pyramid evolves into one foundation pile and two tableau piles. But don't worry if you aren't sure how to play, the computer will remind you when you try to make an illegal play.

216377.overview:
Swiss Connection is a 1-2 player co-operative skiing themed shooter for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Alf Yngve using SEUCK and published by Binary Zone PD in 1991.

In the game, you play an Interpol agent following a trace to the Swiss Apls, where the person suspected to be "Mr. Big" in the biggest drug cartel in Europe is located. You find proof in his house, but his bodyguards discover you! You dash down the mountainside to reach the police station before his thugs can get you. Then you must return with the local police to arrest "Mr. Big" before he leaves the country.

Good luck!

216433.overview:
Skol Äventyret (translates to School Adventure) is a Swedish language text adventure for the Commodore 64 computer. It was developed by Johan Bernkert and published by SYS Public Domain on SYS PD Diskett#21 (1991).

The game itself was made in 1986, but not officially released until 1991.

216437.overview:
Star Klondike (also Known as Loadstar's Klondike Solitaire) is a variation of Klondike solitaire for the Commodore 64. It was developed by John Serafino and published in Loadstar #138 in 1995.

The game has several options, including the ability for drawing 1 or 3 cards, as well as the ability to play either a single-deck or a double-deck version of the game.

216701.overview: Super Cobra is a free public domain unofficial conversion of the arcade classic of the same name for the Commodore 64. It was developed by German coder Jörg Heyltjes of Technische Maschinenfabrik and released in 2008.

216750.overview: Spider Climber is a Spider-Man themed Crazy Climber clone for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Back to the 8 bit and released into the public domain on March 10, 2022. Can you get Spider-Man to the top of the building, so he can stop the criminals?

216814.overview:
The player mans a ground based AA gun. Helicopters and bombers fly overhead dropping paratroopers and bombs. The player must prevent these from landing , when enough of them have made it to earth, they turn into a tank and destroy the players gun. Every shot fired costs points but these can be regained by bringing down aircraft and paratroopers.

The game is actually a ROM hack of the 1983 Rabbit Software game, Paratroopers, but with a change in the background's color, improved SFX, and added music.

216815.overview: A text adventure with graphics created by Fredrik Olsson and released by Compro in 1985.

216816.overview: A rebellion among Santas little helpers has left the funky factory without workers to fulfill the dreams of snotty kids around the world. In a moment of poor judgement you accept to work a shift at the wrapping machine for a bottle of Christmas brew and some candy canes. It is too late to back out now...

216817.overview:
Huge, disgustingly thick, black oil slicks leak in from a fleet of crippled nuclear tankers out in the once lovely, blue Mediterranean Sea! You speed to the rescue in your reclamations sub, the Sea Slug. Avoid the dangerous nuclear wastes and deadly sea crabs. Can you disperse the oil slicks before it's too late? Good luck to you! You're in command of the wonderful Sea. Slug... fastest and Most efficient sub in the ocean! Today the Slug will be put to the ultimate test. You have been sent to destroy nasty black oil slicks dropped into the water from the disabilitated (sic) ship above. Don't allow the oil slicks to touch bottom! While you're about your work, Pockets of nuclear waste and horrible sea crabs wait to destroy you. Avoid them no Matter what! 
 
If you touch either a crab or the pockets of waste... or fail to snatch a slick before it hits bottom, one of your 4 lives will be over! Score 50 points for each oil slick you dispose of.

216818.overview: You are a famous vampire hunter from the old world. You have been given the task of finding and killing the King of the Vampires, Count Dracula! You must search through the country side, killing werewolves, skeletons, and ghouls until you find Dracula. You will need to collect weapons in your search that are able to kill Dracula. You will find guns, silver bullets, garlic, and other items to help you kill him. Every time you fight a Monster, you will lose some energy. To restore your strength you will need to return to your home (the castle in the upper left corner of the map). If your energy level reaches zero, you will die! GOOD LUCK!

216819.overview: Senat is a computerized version of an ancient Egyptian board game of the same name. It was developed by Robert Mundschau and published in Loadstar #148.

216820.overview: This is an odd one, you need to figure out how to serenade your heart's desire. The joystick doesn't work but you can use SPACE BAR to select a Classical piece of music from a menu, random keys play parts of random tunes, F-keys make your lothario stare at the moon (locks the keyboard), and LEFT ARROW quits back to the intro. You have four instruments to choose from, each with its own characteristics.

216821.overview: The adventures of the most famous detective of all time. A fantastic diskette for C/64 containing several cases that will engage our hero. clues, interrogations, tests and, of course... deduction, in the tradition of Sir Arthur Conan Doyle, creator of Sherlock Holmes. On the disk I would find two animated ad ventures; the Lancaster case and the Allan Fox case. In addition to the adventure games, there are also two skill games: Grand Prix and Pistol Race

216822.overview: A puzzle game by Charles Grey and released to the public domain on June 6, 2019. Use your joystick to modify the current image on the left by rotating some lines to match the one on the right as quickly as possible. If time runs out you lose, gain extra points for all time left when you succeed.

216823.overview:
Sirius is an arcade collect-em-up for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Oliver Kirwa with Stefan Siegert providing the music and sound effects. The game was published by Marks & Technik in the following.

•   Happy Computer 1989/04
•   64'er Sonderheft 85

216824.overview: Accept the challenge, overcome the jumps to be the best! Avoid the other skydivers, grab the balloons and press space to open your parachute before the time gets to zero. At zero you meet the ground! A 2018 game from Igor Errazkin, Darro99 and Esteban Palladino.

216825.overview: A single player multi-genre shooter made by Michael John Lalonde (aka Wanderer) with music Richard Bayliss and released in 2006.

216826.overview: A single player action game from the imagination of Jamie Fuller's 6-year-old daughter. Released as part of the Reset64 Magazine 2018 C64 4KB Game Coding Competition.

216827.overview: An unreleased beer-free, Tapper clone for the Commodore 64. The game was developed by Micro Factory.

216828.overview: A racing and gambling game updated from a Swedish game for up to 999 people, this re-release, while it only allowed a measly 5 players included fixes to make it more playable and an English translation.

216829.overview: A fantasy themed platformer from Christian Stenger published by Infomedia in the French language computer journal on diskette, Floopy 64 Nº 12 in 1987.

216830.overview: A two player only, space dueling game created by Ficus.

216831.overview: Space Planters is a new game for the Commodore C64 computer. The game is developed by Wil (code), fieserWolf (music), Logiker, Neyvivi and Wil (pixels). It was originally released in 2020 and later updated Community Edition was released at Vintage Computing Carinthia $16. It was also released as part of the Space Collection for Bobr Games with new music and a new intro screen. Your goal is to create as many high level structures as possible. You get points for each one created and extra points for existing high-level structures so don't bomb them. Confined aliens transform into a strange alien device, 3 or more strange alien devices become an alien spaceship and 3 or more of those an alien space city. Three space rocks become a dwarf planet, three dwarf planets become a telluric planet and 3 of those become a habitable planet. Populate the galaxy!

216832.overview: A PD Uridium style, horizontally scrolling space shooter created by Mark D. Rejhon and released in 1991.

216835.overview:
Spider Fighter is a fixed screen shooter for the Commodore 64. It was coded by Ali Pouladi with graphics also done by Marukpa and Richard Bayliss. Bayliss also did the music as well, It was released into the public domain in 2021.

The game is a re-make of the Atari 2600 game of the same name.

216838.overview:
At C64 compilation of 3 sports games: 
 
    Baseball (2-player side-view baseball game, where players take turns pitching and hitting)
    Football (text-based football competition against the computer, where the player selects their plays from a menu)
    Hockey (2-player 1 - on - 1 hockey competition)

216840.overview: A game by Michael Johnson with music by Richard Bayliss. It is a Space Invaders shooter with Gorf and Galaga influences. Defend earth from alien spiders. If the spiders make it to Earth then the game and civilization along with it, ends.

216841.overview:
An action game created by Derek for the 2020 C64 4KB Game Coding Competition. Collect a brick from the pile. Once all repairs are completed, run back to the flashing pile. Climb a ladder and use left or right when level with a damaged section of chimney to repair it with the brick. Do all repairs.
Watch out for the birds that hill knock you off your ladder. Use the token to scare then off.

216852.overview:
Snodge's Water Caper is a game developed by Richard Bayliss and released in 1995 by Binary Zone PD. Poor Snodge the Biblet... just when we thought things were bad, the worst is yet to come for our poor herd. He has been captured and thrown into the deepest depths of the water. It is up to you to help poor Snodge try and reach the banks of the 4 challenging stages. All is not easy though, as there are deadly creatures that live in the deep water. Luckily for Snodge, he can make bubbles that can kill those deadly creatures. Watch out, as they can fight back! If you are careful enough, you will succeed!

An updated version was made in 1997 using the Shoot 'em Up Construction Kit, which was just titled Water Caper.

216853.overview: Star Stacker is a 1-4 player puzzle game (5 if you want to add a computer controlled player) for the Commodore 64. It was developed by C.E. "Spock" Prince and published in Loadstar #127. Our master copyist's latest brain game pits you against a ruthless computer in a game of colors and shapes. Star Stacker was inspired by a British game called Continuo, and is in some ways similar to Dave Johannsen's Quadrilaton. The computer will play at 3 levels of difficulty: Novice, Expert and Mojo. The program will randomly choose a 4x4 tile of 16 randomly colored squares on the board. The first play is dealt random tile to play. He moves the tile around the play area with the CRSR keys or joystick and drop it anywhere, even on top of a currently placed tile. The player gets a point for every square of his tile that is ON TOP of a currently existing square of the same color. He also gets one point for each square that orthogonally borders a square of the same color that was just placed. Diagonals don't count. You have a choice of 5 different background patterns. F1 for instructions. F2 to change level. F3 to change the Pattern. F4 to toggle players.  F5 for high score list. F6 for color selector. Additionally you can rotate your tile before playing.
