462493.overview: A strange new machine has arrived. Its glowing screen stays hidden behind mysterious barriers: shifting patterns, secret numbers, and even phantom fingerprints. Only the sharpest minds will discover how to break through.

462909.overview: Santa Claus has lost the load of gifts on this snow-covered mountain. He has only a pair of skis and must go down the mountain, avoid obstacles, and reach the gifts! Be careful, he can't miss them!

463456.overview: Serf City is a two-player economics simulation employing both text and graphics. Each player rules one of the valley's two kingdoms, both largely subsistent on wheat crops. Your objective is to increase the size, wealth, and population of your kingdom until you run your opponent out of the valley.

463786.overview:
The program we are presenting now allows us to simulate the operation of a slot machine.

The essential components of a slot machine are three reels—each featuring symbols spaced at regular intervals—and a control mechanism (usually a lever) that sets the reels in motion. When the reels come to a stop, each one displays a symbol to the player. The game involves placing a bet, activating the control to spin the reels, and waiting; a specific payout is awarded based on the resulting combination of the three symbols.

Published in the book "20 Programmi per Commodore 64".

463791.overview:
Strike and Ball is an Italian language text-based sports game for the C64. This program, based on the famous game Mastermind, involves a contest between two players in which each must first choose a secret number and then try to guess the number chosen by their opponent. Players take turns stating a number, and the opponent provides feedback indicating how close that number is to the secret one. This feedback specifies the number of digits that appear in the secret number but in a different position ("ball" digits) and the number of digits that appear in the secret number and occupy the same position in both numbers ("strike" digits). For example, if the secret number is 4371 and the opponent guesses 2357, the response would be 1 "ball" digit (the 7) and 1 "strike" digit (the 3). As the game progresses, it becomes clear that—based on the feedback—some digits must be eliminated from future guesses, others simply need to have their positions changed ("ball" digits), and others, once identified, should not be moved again ("strike" digits). The winner is the first player to correctly guess the opponent's secret number.

It was developed by Franco Arcieri and published as a type-in listing in the book "20 Programmi per Commodore 64".

463905.overview: A single-player run and gun style shooter made using Chris Yates'  shoot em up construction kit by an unknown person and published by Systems Editoriale in 1989.

464062.overview: Robin Hood just won the archery tournament at Nottingham Castle. But as the last of Robin’s three enchanted arrows struck the bullseye, the magic concealing his identity was lost.

464157.overview: Space Control is a 1-player only shooter for the Commodore 64. It was made using Chris Yates' SEUCK engine, and released in 1991 as part of Commodore 64 Club #12 (64/128 Ultra Games)

464341.overview: Santa’s Workout 5 is a puzzle game with one objective: hop off the platforms and close them!

464510.overview: A Simon clone for the Commodore 64, written in BASIC.

464676.overview:
In Sewer, You have to exterminate and stop the waves of rats that are invading the city, starting from the sewer! 

Watch out for their boss too, who appears in front of you every so often! Survive all 30 waves and finish the game.

464723.overview: The aim is to connect the circuits so that all colors run from one circle to the next without any breaks. The lines in each circle can be rotated by moving the green rotating tppl to a circle and pressing fire.

464755.overview:
A winter themed single player game created by Ashley Routledge and David Saunders.

Published in Commodore Disk User 1989/01-02, Commodore Zone Issue #12, Commodore Force #02 (February 1993) - Reel Action #4

464883.overview: You are a little, white rabbit; lost and hungry. You are in a garden and can smell carrots; once you've eaten one you want more and more.

465030.overview:
Row row row your boat gently down the the stream...

Not this time! You have a speed boat instead of the row boat. It isn’t too difficult to navigate at first, just use the two cursor keys to steer left and right. Throughout the river are points, by guiding the boat over these, you will build up a score. After a score of 1000 the river will narrow. At 2000 it narrows still more. As well as the points in the water there are logs. Hitting these will get you as far as taking the boat to shore will... nowhere.

465725.overview: A single-player side scrolling space shooter for the C64. It was developed and released by TND using the sideways SEUCK mod in 2020 as part of that year's SEUCK competition.

466243.overview:
SLOTSHOT is a unique blend of puzzle and shooter mechanics designed for the Commodore 64.
The player's task is to fill the columns of blocks moving to the left in order to eliminate them. As you progress, the speed at which the wall moves increases, requiring you to think faster and fill in the gaps more quickly. It is also worth remembering that yellow blocks always fit into the second free space. The game ends when the wall reaches the player's block launcher.

466481.overview:
Slap Shot (not to be confused with Slap-Shot! Hockey/Slapshot) is a 2 player only vs 2 on 2 (player and a goalie) hockey game for the Commodore 64. It was developed by John Fedor and published in COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1989/10 (Issue #76). 
 
The score’s five up and time is running out—only 20 seconds left. Your opponent is pushing the puck up the ice, trying desperately to get around you. But this time, your defenses are impenetrable. Suddenly, a mistake—the puck slides free. You grab it and race for the goal. A glance at the clock: five, four, three.... You fake right and then shoot left. The goalie lunges, but to no avail. The puck’s in the net— you win!

“Slap Shot” is a two-player, arcade-style game requiring quick reflexes. The object of the game is simple: Using two players, a goalie and a forward, you must outscore your opponent in a game of ice hockey. Slap Shot features many of the aspects of this sport, including checking and a puck that sometimes leaves the surface of the ice. Two game options are also provided; games can be based on time and on the number of goals scored.

466613.overview: Contains Pharaoh pinball, Space pinball, Spy pinball

468316.overview:
The New Dimension in co-op with Blazon is very proud to present SPIDER MAZE 2. A fun sequel to its cute arcade predecessor, which was first launched in 2018.
The player's task is to collect all the diamonds on the board within a specified time. Taking a light bulb illuminates our hero, making him immune to spider bites for a short time. In later levels, there will be spikes that cannot be stepped on and hearts that add new life. The letter B adds bonus points, and the watch adds time.

469257.overview:
Santa la Vista is a single-player Breakout variant with a Christmas theme for the Commodore 64.

Instead of removing bricks from the screen like a traditional Breakout game, your goal is to ruin Christmas for everyone and remove presents from Santa's sleigh.

The game was developed and released by Zapac Software on December 19, 2020.

469408.overview: The player's task is to collect all the diamonds on the board. Taking a light bulb illuminates our hero, making him immune to spider bites for a short time. In later levels, skulls will appear, which cannot be entered, and hearts that add new life.

469466.overview: A space shooter developed by Gaetano Chiummo using the Shoot 'Em Up Construction Kit and released in 1991 by Sea Software.

469477.overview: Shoot and Blast is a single-player SEUCK made shooter developed by Gaetano Chiummo and published by Sea Software in 1991.

469479.overview: Super Bruno III is the third game in the Super Bruno series of Shoot 'em UP Construction Kit games for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Gaetano Chiummo and published by Sea Software in 1991.

469480.overview: Super Bruno 2 is the second game in the Super Bruno series of Shoot 'em UP Construction Kit games for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Gaetano Chiummo and published by Sea Software in 1981.

469482.overview: Super Bruno is a one player SEUCK shooter developed by Gaetano Chiummo and published by Sea Software in 1991.

469810.overview:
Based on the original SLALOM game
by COMMODORE ELEC. LTD & HAL LABORATORY, JAPAN

The Winter Olympics may have ended, but the pleasures of skiing continue on the COMMODORE 64 with SUPER SLALOM, a revamped edition of the legendary Commodore/Hal game originally created for the Japan-only MAX MACHINE. This time you're in for remade colourful graphics, a new OST full of diverse tracks, enhanced gameplay and six different slopes (compared to the repeated couple of slopes of the original) created from scratch. 

And, to be true to this "SKI FOREVER" motto, SUPER SLALOM also includes a full fledged LEVEL EDITOR! 

In a SEUCK fashion, use your joystick and/or keyboard to easily access all the core features of the editor. Draw your slopes with a joystick, put the hazards, tune the difficulty. Choose between ten scenarios and eleven different soundtracks to create the perfect mix-and-match for each of the six unique slopes. Save it to disk, both as re-editable data and as a standalone game. Or, just take the vanilla SUPER SLALOM data and customize it, make it easier, harder, weirder. Or... just play SUPER SLALOM as a standalone game and have fun dropping crazy high scores.

470009.overview: The secret recipes have been stolen and scattered all across Cocktail Land. Help the Superstar Chefs recover them in a vibrant world filled with cartoon-style creatures, fruit, and hidden treasures.

470229.overview: A little snake game made when learning C64 assembly language. Still very much a work in progress, albeit playable.

470338.overview: Space Invaders on the original arcade hardware moved objects by directly manipulating pixels. That works, but it’s computationally expensive — and the arcade CPU was twice as fast as the one in a C64. Not exactly a good approach for a port.

470749.overview: A homebrewed C64 Snake coded entirely in BASIC. Developed by CDIS Lab (a dev studio based in Turkey) and released into the public domain on January 19, 2026.

470805.overview: Space Invaders for the Commodore 64 has, of course, been done before.

470811.overview:
Scorpion-II is a computerized version of the solitaire card game Scorpion for the Commodore 64. This version was developed by Darrell G. Rose.Had a hard day? Bored? Looking for areal challenge? What could be better than a quiet game of solitaire?

“Scorpion II” offers not only the challenge for which solitaire is noted, but also tricky new moves and excellent machine language animation. Published in the following: 

- COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1988/10 (Issue #64)

- Best of Gazette 1988 (Disk Issue)

471278.overview:
Gsp Greek Teams Mod For Soccer Boss
The game starts with selecting any team from 4 divisions. You can also create your own team once you reach the last division. Once you have selected a team (or created your own) you will start in Division 4. The original game was based off the British FA Cup with 20 teams per division.

471279.overview: Beat the sands of time or get crushed!

471666.overview: A brand new classic Klondike solitaire card game for the Commodore 64 which is simply good to play

472138.overview:
Welcome to Shadowvault, a roguelike adventure for the Commodore 64. Descend into the ever-shifting depths of the Shadowvault, uncover ancient lore, and master the power of forbidden contracts.

Key Mechanics:

•   Permadeath: Death ends your run immediately.
•   Skill Progression: Skills raise dynamically during combat, improving weapon proficiency and survivability.
•   Equipment Tiers: Weapons and armor grow stronger on deeper floors (bonuses scale 1–5).
•   Fog of War: Only see a 7-tile radius around you. Explore carefully to avoid ambushes.

472487.overview: Each dungeon level is part of a fractured interdimensional maze. There are no stairs back — only a clue hidden somewhere in the darkness. Find it, open the gate, and descend deeper toward the relic.

472573.overview:
STREET SPORTS POGO challenges you in various ways: Build up power for
your jump, focus for the perfect lift-off angle and keep a cool head during the
landing phase.

472759.overview: Sparkly needs to connect all the leds on th ePCB, from + to minus. The clock is ticking and Sparkly can only stop at connections so plan your route.

474136.overview: Super Alien is a single-screen action game. The player moves through the maze and can place traps on the floor. When a monster walks into it, it becomes trapped and the player can kill it by filling in the hole. Each defeated monster rewards points while touching them results in a life loss. The maze is shown from the usual top-down perspective, but the characters have a side-view.

474243.overview: Spellbound is a fantasy role-playing game for the Commodore 64 that allows players to explore a mystical land, battle enemies, and interact with various characters. It is known for its atmospheric world-building and traditional RPG mechanics typical of the mid-1980s.

475036.overview: In this game, the soccer pitch becomes a deadly battleground. Weaponize your ball to smash killer robots, take down opposing human players, and blast goals into the net to rack up massive points. Bring your friends, watch the rebounds, and fight to survive!

475039.overview: The research station Elysium drifts dark and silent - nineteen days after something went very wrong. Its forty-seven crew are dead. You wake from cryo-sleep with no memory, a failing reactor below you, and perhaps an hour before it takes the whole station with it.

475993.overview: THE SECRET OF BARRON WOOD is a supernatural short story in the form of a text adventure.  Venture into the deep wood and explore its darkest recesses, where a century-old secret awaits your discovery.

477217.overview: Welcome to Skittles, a classical single player chessboard puzzle game. You have just one pawn, move it to capture all other pawns on the board. Start by choosing the pawn type: you can be a tower, a bishop or a knight. The game is easy if you are a bishop or a tower, being a knight is much harder. There're 8 easy levels and 8 hard ones, you must complete all of them. Higher levels, either easy or hard, have more pawns and get more complicated. There is one king at each level, this is the last pawn you have to capture. Don't waste your moves, they're limited. Try to capture pawns at every step.

477461.overview: Seeing a full game for the Oric Atmos in just 10 lines of BASIC, I was inspired to re-implement it for the Commodore 64 and expand on it a little making use of that machine's features.

478317.overview: An original game for the Commodore 64, written in 6502 assembly.

478547.overview: Another chess puzzle game, that requires memory and attention skills. Pick the right white tower first and try to capture 7 different black pieces. Go for 1 pawn, 1 rook, 1 bishop, 1 king, 1 queen & 2 knights (left/right facing). You cannot attack the same type of piece two times, make a plan before you start. You have limited time for every puzzle, choose a slow (more time) or fast pace. 9 puzzles to beat the game. The higher  the level the less time is available. You may abandon the current puzzle and start over with a new, random one. There are over a hundred puzzles for you to complete, good luck!

479007.overview:
Shikaku is a relaxing Japanese logic puzzle game, now available for the Commodore 64.

The goal is simple: divide the board into rectangles so that each rectangle contains exactly one number, and its area matches that number. Easy to learn, but increasingly challenging as the puzzles become more complex.

479501.overview: Your line never stops and never goes straight — it's always curving, and all you control is which way. Steer left, steer right, and don't touch anything: your own trail, your opponent's, or the walls are all lethal. Every trail opens brief gaps as it draws — sneak through one to escape a trap or cut off your rival. First to 5 rounds takes the match.

479722.overview: Sixies is a fast-paced Commodore 64 puzzle game where players place, rotate, and merge dice across a compact grid.

479836.overview:
You scrapped the Mastervader.   Nobody thanked you. The meltdown followed. Nothing in the yard makes power any more. An original arcade climb for the Commodore 64, written in 6502 assembly.
One player, or two at once.

479838.overview: Steer the serpent, eat apples, and clear 12 handcrafted arenas that loop ever faster. Walls block but never kill. Hit one head-on and the snake waits (losing 1 point per beat) until you steer away; travel along a wall while pressing into it and the snake slides, snapping into the first gap that passes. Only two things end a life: biting yourself, and the ghosts.

479874.overview:
Stock Inc. is a text-based stock market simulation from the Commodore 64. It supports up to 8 players (with a minimum of 2, as there is no computer opponent)

It was developed and released as a freeware game by Sean Huxter in 1985.

480079.overview: In this series of puzzles, a chessboard is filled with black pawns. You need to replace all these pawns with the ones on the left. The 63 pawns on the left are colored and organized into 21 sets of 3. You cannot change the order within each triplet, but you can rotate it. Place all triplets so that their colors match those of the chessboard. You can clear the chessboard at any time and start over from the beginning. You may also reposition a triplet on the chessboard, if you change your mind. 30 puzzles to beat the game. Each one of them has a unique solution.

480092.overview: A tiny arcade game for the Commodore 64. The floor is scrolling away beneath you — don't get sucked in!

480330.overview: A SEUCK based shooter for one or two players created by the French developers DXCH in 1988, music by Chris Huelsbeck.

480489.overview:
Ruote Fumanti (smokin tyres) is a Commodore 64 game. A 24 KB program that runs on a stock PAL machine: a real C64, a flashcart, any emulator. No memory expansions. 
 
Eight stages, flat out

The traffic does not move over for you: you overtake it, you shunt it off the road, or you land on top of it. The fords cannot be driven around, they have to be jumped, and you need ninety-five miles an hour to leave the ground. Some stages have rock ravines instead of water, and if you go in the car shrinks away as it falls. The winter stages have ice.
Seven seconds with the police

In the last stretch of every stage the traffic clears out and a police car comes up behind you. One against one, with the jump disabled. You hold your line, or you push it off the road, which is the thing that pays best in the whole game.
On the panel

Score, miles per hour, cars left, hits, time. How much of the course you have done, as a percentage. And a JUMP OK light, on when you are going fast enough to take off. The readouts are sprites, so they never wobble with the scrolling.

480493.overview: The battle of the kings: everyone on the chessboard, only half will remain. Start with whichever one, gather 6 pawns and attack another king within 7 moves. An attack with fewer pieces will fail. No more than 7 moves are allowed. You cannot choose the same king twice,  nor return to an empty square. Kings of the same color are allies and must not fight each other. At the end of the battle, the pawns have been captured and only 8 kings survive. 10 puzzles to complete, you may restart the current puzzle at any time. To win, devise a plan before making any move. each puzzle has a unique solution.

480543.overview: Deep beneath the ruins of Daedaloff’s tower lie ancient scrolls of great power. Find seven scrolls to save the tower.

480650.overview: Goal: Move The Big Red Block To The Bottom Center. Blocks Must Not Overlap.

480652.overview: A Commodore 64 reimplementation (i.e. clone) of the mechanics of Mega-Bug (Tandy 26-3076, 1982, Steve Bjork; itself a port of Bob Bishop's Dung Beetles). This game, "Slop Beetle" named for its provenance: the code, the art and the tune were all written by a language model.

480734.overview: Snake's Snack is a retro game written by Alberto (BCO) Sgaggero in BASIC V2 for the fantastic Commodore 64.

481071.overview: Save the last humanoids on the planet from being captured by aliens. Shoot their captors and return them back to the planet's surface. Complete increasingly difficult attack waves. If you're surrounded, release a smart bomb to destroy everyhing in sight. The portal will teleport you to the nearest human in distress. You can also warp ahead through it if you have 4 humanoids with you.

481292.overview: Companion assembly sources for Starbraze, Volume 1 of the C64 Game Manual Series by Eric A. Norton and Jorah Sallow.

481404.overview: SRAM, the adventure game from ERE Informatique released in 1986 on Amstrad CPC, is coming to Commodore 64

481761.overview: The fifth skittles series part features two classic chess-style problems. The problem of independence in which no piece threatens another. And the problem of domination where the pieces must control every square. Choose the game type and try to position all the pieces accordingly. If time runs out you start over from the level you were on. Playground allows you to create puzzles by placing pieces on an empty board. Problems such as the eight queens puzzle are included in a set of 10 levels. Each puzzle has multiple solutions. you only need to find one.

481839.overview: A falling-block puzzle game for the Commodore 64, about blocks that grab each other.

481928.overview: You wake in the entrance hall of a house that rearranges itself around you. There is no map to find — the map is the thing you make, one room at a time, by picking rooms up and putting them down somewhere better. Walk through a door and you are in the next room. Press TAB and the room becomes the plan of the whole house:  a grid you can lift from and place into. Everything inside a room travels with it — the fire, the water, the guard, the thing in the corner. Move the library next to the oven and you will find out what that means.

481942.overview: Swap two sweets, line up three, and watch the board go **pop**. Line up four and you get a **striped candy** that wipes out a whole row. Make an L and you get a **wrapped candy** that blows up everything around it. Line up five and you get the **colour bomb** — swap it with any candy and every candy of that colour on the board disappears at once.

482038.overview: A new graffiti game for the Commodore 64.It’s 1983 and every wall in New York is waiting for your name. Type in your tag and watch it get sprayed across the bricks, never the same way twice. Then hit the streets with five cans and five nights to get up.

482044.overview: MVT Computers presents STELLA 7, a scrolling space shooter for the Commodore 64. You pilot a lone fighter low over a hostile planet, destroy wave after wave of alien attackers, and refuel in deep rock caves before your tanks run dry.

482073.overview: Steel Ranger 2 is the sequel to the side-scrolling action adventure from 2018, inspired by Turrican and Metroid.

482199.overview:
Black border. Black background. Black walls. And you are black too.

The only things you can see are what a guard's lamp falls on, and the darkness that hides the room from you also hides you from them. Every room of Grey Holt castle holds one treasure, glinting purple in the dark. Take it, find the door, walk out.

Play it alone: one thief, fifteen rooms, a par time for each and a rank after every room. Or bring a friend: two thieves, one joystick each, one castle full of lamps.

482290.overview: Chapter 1: Beyond the Gate is a free point-and-click adventure for the Commodore 64, in English and German. It is the first chapter of a series.

482601.overview: This is a port/remaster of Sabre Wulf, Ultimate’s 1984 classic, reimagined for the Commodore 64.

482610.overview:
A remote station orbiting the Moon has stopped responding. You arrive to find its security AI in control and the crew turned into armed sentries.

Fight your way from the docking bays through medical wards, research labs, reactor decks and overgrown hydroponics. Search the side rooms for supplies, reach the Bridge and terminate the hostile signal.

482751.overview: A colourful platform adventure for the Commodore 64

482766.overview: Fight through Wild Jungle, Dark Swamp, Deep Sea, Star Zone, Catacombs and Hell Gate. Every world has its own colours, music scale and boss: REX, HYDRA, KRAKEN, STAR ROCKET, BONE KING and DEMON LORD. The six worlds repeat three times (18 levels), and every round gets harder.

482771.overview: SCOTOGNO SOCCER is a football game (a bit of a mess) seen from above, one against one, for the Commodore 64. Play alone against the computer or challenge a friend on the same C64: one joystick each, one ball, no mercy.

482828.overview: A brand-new horizontally scrolling shoot-’em-up for the Commodore 64, in the spirit of Gradius, Sanxion and Delta. Fly the lone STARFALL interceptor through six hostile worlds, blast your way past each world’s guardian, and take the fight all the way to the heart of the invasion: The Enemy Core.

482910.overview: An endless climb for the Commodore 64. Carry the last flame to Heaven's Gate.

482924.overview: The tiles are drawn in hires, a hardware sprite cursor glides over the board, the tiles fall and the columns slide one tile at a time, and there are sound effects for every action.
